definition_zh: 人口增长；（生物）种群增长
definition_en: an increase in the number of people or organisms in a place or group
core_image: 一条曲线从左下角缓缓抬头，随后几乎竖直向上冲出图纸
scene: 这里指「人口增长」。 Rapid population growth outpaced the city's water supply.
sceneCN: 这里 population growth 指「人口数量的增加」（第 1 个义项：某地人口总数上升）；句意为人口的快速增长超出了城市供水能力。图中可辨识物件：陡升的曲线、拥挤的楼群、见底的水塔、逐年刻度。

pos.zh: 人口增长；种群增长（不可数，偶作可数指具体一次增长）

forms.label: 复数（少见，指多次局部增长）

senses.title: More people in a place
senses.definition: a rise in the number of people living in a place
senses.definitionCN: 某地居住人数的上升
senses.example: Rapid population growth outpaced the city's water supply.
senses.exampleCN: 人口的快速增长超出了城市供水能力。
senses.why: population names the people counted together, and growth names increase, so the phrase states a simplest fact: the count is going up.
senses.whyCN: population 指被一起计数的人，growth 指增加，因此这个短语陈述一件最简单的事：数目在上升。

senses.title: The rate of increase
senses.titleCN: 增长率：单位时间增加多少
senses.definition: the percentage or number by which a population rises in a given period
senses.definitionCN: 一定时期内人口上升的百分比或数量
senses.example: The population growth rate fell from three percent to one.
senses.exampleCN: 人口增长率从百分之三降到百分之一。
senses.why: once demographers wanted to compare places, the phrase needed a denominator, and rate supplies it.
senses.whyCN: 当人口学家需要比较各地，这个短语就需要一个分母，rate 提供了它。

senses.title: Natural increase
senses.definition: growth produced by births exceeding deaths, without migration
senses.definitionCN: 出生数超过死亡数所带来的增长，不计迁移
senses.example: Natural population growth turned negative as births fell.
senses.exampleCN: 随着出生数下降，人口自然增长转为负值。
senses.why: demographers separate the two books that change a population, and natural increase is the one kept without migration.
senses.whyCN: 人口学家把改变人口的两本账分开，自然增长就是不计迁移的那一本。

senses.title: Growth through migration
senses.definition: growth produced by more people arriving than leaving
senses.definitionCN: 迁入人数多于迁出人数所带来的增长
senses.example: Most of the city's population growth came from newcomers rather than births.
senses.exampleCN: 这座城市的人口增长多来自外来者，而非出生。
senses.why: the second book is net migration, and a city can grow through arrivals even when its own birth rate is low.
senses.whyCN: 第二本账是净迁移：即使本地出生率很低，城市也能靠迁入而增长。

senses.title: The steep phase of a curve
senses.titleCN: 指数增长阶段：曲线陡升
senses.definition: the phase in which numbers rise faster and faster because growth feeds on itself
senses.definitionCN: 数量因增长自身而越来越快地上升的阶段
senses.example: During the steep phase of population growth, schools were built every year.
senses.exampleCN: 在人口增长的陡升阶段，每年都要新建学校。
senses.why: growth that feeds on itself bends the curve upward, which is why the phrase is often used with steep and exponential.
senses.whyCN: 自我推动的增长把曲线向上掰弯，因此这个短语常与 steep、exponential 连用。

senses.title: Growth of non-human populations
senses.definition: an increase in the numbers of animals, plants or microbes rather than people
senses.definitionCN: 指动物、植物或微生物数量的增加，而非人口
senses.example: Deer population growth followed the removal of predators.
senses.exampleCN: 捕食者消失之后，鹿群数量随之增长。
senses.why: the same arithmetic governs animals, so population growth is also the standard term in ecology.
senses.whyCN: 同一套算术也管动物，因此 population growth 同样是生态学的标准术语。

senses.title: The end of growth
senses.titleCN: 零增长或负增长：增长的终止
senses.definition: the condition in which numbers stop rising, as in zero population growth
senses.definitionCN: 数量停止上升的状态，如人口零增长
senses.example: Zero population growth was reached in the 1990s.
senses.exampleCN: 人口零增长在 1990 年代实现。
senses.why: once growth became a policy variable, its absence needed a name, and zero growth supplies the target.
senses.whyCN: 一旦增长成为政策变量，它的缺席也需要一个名称，零增长正好提供这个目标。

senses.title: Growth of a market or audience
senses.titleCN: 经济义：市场或受众规模的扩大
senses.definition: an increase in the number of customers or users seen as a population
senses.definitionCN: 把客户或用户视作人群时的数量扩大
senses.example: The app's population growth attracted advertisers.
senses.exampleCN: 这款应用用户规模的增长吸引了广告商。
senses.why: business counts users as a population, so the phrase transfers without changing its arithmetic.
senses.whyCN: 商业把用户当作人群来计数，因此这个短语在转用时算术并未改变。

intro.en: Population comes from Latin populatio 'a peopling', from populus 'people'; growth is native English from grow. The phrase is modern. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: population 来自拉丁 populatio「使有人居住、人群」，源自 populus「人民」；growth 是英语本族词，来自 grow。这个短语是近代组合。年代均为约数。

items.en: Populus meant 'people, nation'. Its own origin is uncertain; the proposal that it came through Etruscan is a hypothesis rather than a demonstrated derivation.
items.cn: populus 意为「人民、民族」。其自身来源不确定；认为它经埃特鲁里亚语而来的说法属假说，并非已证实的派生。

items.en: Populatio named a peopling or a multitude; English took population in the sixteenth century for the people of a place.
items.cn: populatio 指使有人居住或人群；英语在 16 世纪以 population 指某地的人口。

items.en: Grow descends from Old English growan 'to grow, increase', of Germanic stock, and its noun growth followed in the fourteenth century.
items.cn: grow 承自古英语 growan「生长、增加」，属日耳曼语；其名词 growth 于 14 世纪出现。

items.en: Population growth became a fixed phrase in the nineteenth century, when censuses made the count comparable across decades.
items.cn: population growth 在 19 世纪成为固定短语，当时人口普查使跨年代的计数可以比较。

items.en: The twentieth century turned the phrase into a subject of policy, from Malthus's arithmetic to the population conferences of the 1990s.
items.cn: 20 世纪把这个短语变成政策议题，从马尔萨斯的算术到 1990 年代的人口会议。

items.en: Source uncertain (first dates): the earliest use of the exact phrase is not precisely recorded, and the origin of Latin populus remains unsettled.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代）：这一确切短语的最早使用没有精确记录；拉丁 populus 的来源仍无定论。

note.en: Group one holds words of the populus family that are easily confused; group two holds phrases for numbers rising.
note.cn: 第一组是同出 populus 词族、容易混淆的词；第二组是数量上升的其他说法。

entries.definition: The number of people or organisms; population growth is the change in that number over time.
entries.definitionCN: 指人或生物的数量；population growth 是这个数量随时间的变化。

entries.definition: Full of people, as a populous country; it describes a state, not a trend.
entries.definitionCN: 指人口众多，如人口大国；描述状态，不描述趋势。

entries.definition: To fill a place with people or to enter data into a system; it names an act, not a trend.
entries.definitionCN: 指使人居住于某地或向系统填入数据；命名动作，而非趋势。

entries.definition: De- 'away from' plus population: the losing of people from a place, the mirror image of growth.
entries.definitionCN: de-「离开」加 population：某地失去人口，是增长的镜像。

entries.definition: A neutral statement that the number has risen, without implying a rate or a phase.
entries.definitionCN: 中性说明数量已上升，不含速率或阶段的意味。

entries.definition: Growth described through births, deaths and age structure rather than a single total.
entries.definitionCN: 通过出生、死亡与年龄结构描述的 growth，而非单一总量。

entries.definition: A short surge in births; it is one cause of population growth, not the general term.
entries.definitionCN: 指出生数的短促激增；它是人口增长的一个原因，而非总称。

entries.definition: The largest population an environment can support; growth stops when it is reached.
entries.definitionCN: 指环境能支撑的最大人口量；达到它时增长就停止。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: population 'the people counted' + growth 'increase': the count going up.
normal.cn: population「被计数的人口」+ growth「增加」：数目在上升。

normal.en: The family runs population, populous, populate, depopulation, growth, grow.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 population、populous、populate、depopulation、growth、grow。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the senses: population growth rate, natural population growth, zero population growth.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出各义项：人口增长率、人口自然增长、人口零增长。

normal.en: Demographers split growth into natural increase and net migration.
normal.cn: 人口学家把增长拆成自然增加与净迁移。

normal.en: Growth without a rate is a fact; growth with a rate is a comparison.
normal.cn: 不带速率的增长是事实；带速率的增长是比较。

abstract.en: Picture a line on paper that bends upward and will not straighten.
abstract.cn: 想象纸上的线向上弯，弯得收不回来。

abstract.en: Picture a lifeboat taking on people faster than it can take on water.
abstract.cn: 想象救生艇上人的增加快过它能进水的速度。

abstract.en: Picture a queue that doubles while the door stays one door wide.
abstract.cn: 想象队伍不断翻倍，而门始终只有一扇宽。

examples.en: Population growth slowed once girls stayed in school longer.
examples.cn: 女孩在校时间延长后，人口增长放缓了。

examples.en: The graph shows population growth against grain output.
examples.cn: 这张图把人口增长与粮食产量并列显示。

examples.en: Wildlife population growth can overshoot the food supply.
examples.cn: 野生动物种群的增长可能超过食物供给。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「population（人口）+ growth（增长）」——被计数的人越来越多 → 人口增长

root: 拉丁 populus「人民」（更早来源不确定）+ populatio「人群、使有人居住」+ 古英语 growan「生长、增加」；英语 population growth。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one movement: a count rises, and that rise is then read as a rate, a natural surplus, a migration effect, a steep curve, a wildlife trend, a halt, and a market.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个变化展开：某个计数上升，这个上升再被读成速率、自然盈余、迁移效应、陡升曲线、野生动物趋势、停止，以及市场。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a curve that lifts gently and then shoots upward.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条先缓抬、后猛冲的曲线。

branches.en: FACT AND RATE: the bare increase, then the same increase divided by time.
branches.cn: 事实与速率：先是不加修饰的增加，再是除以时间后的同一增加。

branches.en: TWO SOURCES: births exceeding deaths, or arrivals exceeding departures.
branches.cn: 两个来源：出生多于死亡，或迁入多于迁出。

branches.en: SELF-FEEDING GROWTH: the steep phase, whether of people or of deer.
branches.cn: 自我推动的增长：陡升阶段，人或鹿皆然。

branches.en: THE HALT: zero growth is the phrase turned into a target.
branches.cn: 停止：零增长就是把短语变成目标。

branches.en: BORROWED MARKET: users are counted as a population and their rise becomes growth.
branches.cn: 借用的市场：用户被当作人群计数，其上升便成为增长。

intro.en: The phrase joins a Latin noun of people to a native English noun of increasing; neither half carries a prefix or suffix of its own.
intro.cn: 这个短语把表示人民的拉丁名词与表示增加的本族英语名词并置；两半本身都不带前缀或后缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin populus yields population, populous, populate and depopulation; Old English growan yields grow, growth and growing.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 populus 衍生 population、populous、populate 与 depopulation；古英语 growan 衍生 grow、growth 与 growing。

items.example: The Latin noun names a people as a body.
items.exampleCN: 这个拉丁名词把人民视为一个整体。

items.example: The delta is the most populous region.
items.exampleCN: 三角洲是人口最稠密的地区。

items.example: Settlers populated the valley within a century.
items.exampleCN: 定居者在一个世纪内住满了这条谷地。

items.example: The town grew along the river.
Population growth outpaced the water supply.
items.exampleCN: 人口增长超出了供水能力。

items.example: A growing population needs more housing.
items.exampleCN: 不断增长的人口需要更多住房。

definition_zh: 生物风化；岩石因生物活动而破碎或分解的过程
definition_en: the breakdown of rock caused by living organisms, whether by mechanical force or by the acids they release
core_image: 地衣在裸岩表面摊开一层灰绿色的壳，根须顺着细缝往下钻，缝边的岩石已经发酥
scene: 裸岩表面铺着一层灰绿色的地衣，细缝里伸进几缕根须，缝口的岩屑一碰就落，老师说 Biological weathering starts on bare rock long before any soil can form.
sceneCN: 这里 biological weathering 指「岩石因生物活动而破碎或分解的过程」，取第 1 个义项（总称）；句意为生物风化在土壤形成之前很久就在裸岩上开始了。图中可辨识物件：地衣、根须、岩缝、岩屑。

pos.zh: 生物风化（不可数，地质学与地理学用语）

derivatives.zh: 从生物学角度；在生物意义上

senses.title: Life breaking down rock
senses.definition: any weathering in which a living organism provides the force, the acid or both
senses.definitionCN: 由生物提供力量、酸或两者兼有的任何风化过程
senses.example: Biological weathering is the first step in turning bare lava into living soil.
senses.exampleCN: 生物风化是把裸露熔岩变成有生命的土壤的第一步。
senses.why: The label names the agent, not the mechanism, which is why the same process can sit between physical and chemical weathering.
senses.whyCN: 这个标签命名的是施力者而非机制，因此同一过程可以夹在物理风化与化学风化之间。

senses.title: Roots prising joints open
senses.definition: roots growing into cracks and widening them as they thicken
senses.definitionCN: 根系长进裂缝，随着变粗而把裂缝撑大
senses.example: Root wedging is biological weathering with a purely mechanical effect.
senses.exampleCN: 根劈作用是一种效果纯属机械的生物风化。
senses.why: A root exerts pressure like a wedge, so the rock breaks without any change in its minerals.
senses.whyCN: 根像楔子一样施加压力，因此岩石被撑破而矿物并不改变。

senses.title: Lichen and moss acids
senses.definition: organic acids from lichens and mosses dissolving minerals at the rock surface
senses.definitionCN: 地衣与苔藓分泌的有机酸溶解岩石表层的矿物
senses.example: Lichen acids are biological weathering that also happens to be chemical.
senses.exampleCN: 地衣酸造成的生物风化，同时也属于化学风化。
senses.why: The organism supplies the acid, so the category follows the agent while the mechanism is dissolution.
senses.whyCN: 酸由生物提供，因此分类跟随施力者，而机制其实是溶解。

senses.title: Animals mixing and digging
senses.definition: burrowing, trampling and wallowing that expose fresh rock and disturb the soil
senses.definitionCN: 穴居、踩踏与打滚使新鲜岩石暴露并扰动土壤
senses.example: Burrowing animals speed up biological weathering by opening the ground.
senses.exampleCN: 穴居动物通过把地面翻开，加快了生物风化。
senses.why: Digging does not dissolve anything, but it breaks the protective crust and lets water and air in.
senses.whyCN: 挖掘本身并不溶解任何东西，但它破坏保护性结皮，让水和空气进入。

senses.title: Microbes and algae
senses.definition: bacteria and algae that dissolve minerals, accumulate salts and hold water against the rock
senses.definitionCN: 细菌与藻类溶解矿物、积累盐分并让水停留在岩石表面
senses.example: Microbes carry out biological weathering inside the pores of the stone.
senses.exampleCN: 微生物在石材孔隙内部进行生物风化。
senses.why: Their waste products are acids and chelating compounds, so the smallest organisms can do the most persistent work.
senses.whyCN: 它们的代谢产物是酸与螯合物，因此最小的生物反而能做最持久的功。

senses.title: Swelling and shrinking by plants
senses.titleCN: 植物吸水与失水引起的胀缩
senses.definition: wet roots and stems swelling in pores, then contracting and loosening the surrounding rock
senses.definitionCN: 湿润的根与茎在孔隙中膨胀，随后收缩并把周围岩石松脱
senses.example: Water uptake and loss add a slow biological weathering to the cliff.
senses.exampleCN: 水的吸收与散失给崖壁添上一种缓慢的生物风化。
senses.why: Repeated swelling and shrinking works like a many-small wedges, each one widening what the last one loosened.
senses.whyCN: 反复胀缩就像许多小楔子，每一个都把上一个弄松的地方再扩开一点。

senses.title: Damage to stone monuments
senses.definition: the same organisms growing on carved stone and destroying its surface and inscriptions
senses.definitionCN: 同一类生物长在雕琢过的石头上，破坏其表面与铭文
senses.example: Conservators treat biological weathering as a serious threat to the inscriptions.
senses.exampleCN: 文物保护人员把生物风化视为对铭文的严重威胁。
senses.why: Because carved stone is a cultural record rather than a natural outcrop, the term moved into conservation with a sense of loss.
senses.whyCN: 由于雕石是文化记录而非天然露头，这个词进入文物保护领域时便带上「损失」的意味。

senses.title: Boring and scraping by marine life
senses.definition: shellfish, worms and grazing animals that bore into or scrape away coastal rock
senses.definitionCN: 贝类、蠕虫与食藻动物钻入或刮去海岸岩石
senses.example: Boring clams perform biological weathering along the whole shoreline.
senses.exampleCN: 钻孔蛤沿着整条海岸线进行生物风化。
senses.why: On coasts the biological damage is measurable in cubic metres, so the term is used with the same confidence as for frost.
senses.whyCN: 在海岸，生物造成的破坏可以用立方米计量，因此这个词用在潮间带时与用于霜冻时同样确定。

intro.en: Biological derives from Greek bios life plus logos study, through French biologie. Weathering is the native English noun from Old English weder. The compound label belongs to twentieth-century earth science.
intro.cn: biological 出自希腊 bios「生命」加 logos「研究」，经法语 biologie 传入。weathering 是英语本族名词，来自古英语 weder。这个复合标签属于二十世纪的地球科学。

items.en: Bios meant life and the span of a life, and it supplies the bio- element in biology, biography and biosphere.
items.cn: bios 意为生命与一生的长度，是 biology、biography 与 biosphere 中 bio- 成分的来源。

items.en: Logos meant word, account or reasoned study, and the ending -logy names a field of inquiry rather than a thing.
items.cn: logos 意为语词、叙述或理性研究，词尾 -logy 命名的是一个研究领域，而不是某个实物。

items.en: The compound biologie is recorded in French around the turn of the nineteenth century, and English biology followed soon after.
items.cn: 复合词 biologie 在十九世纪之交出现于法语书证，英语 biology 紧随其后。

items.en: The adjective ending -ical comes from Latin -alis, so biological means relating to the study of life.
items.cn: 形容词词尾 -ical 来自拉丁 -alis，因此 biological 意为「与生命研究有关的」。

items.en: Twentieth-century soil science and conservation set biological weathering beside the physical and chemical kinds, naming the agent rather than the mechanism.
items.cn: 二十世纪的土壤学与文物保护把生物风化与物理、化学两类并列，命名的是施力者而非机制。

note.en: Group one holds the sibling weathering categories; group two holds biological processes that are not weathering.
note.cn: 第一组是并列的风化类别；第二组是并非风化的生物过程。

entries.definition: Breakdown by force with the minerals unchanged; roots can cause it while the category stays physical.
entries.definitionCN: 由力量造成的破碎、矿物不变；根系可造成它，而类别仍属物理风化。

entries.definition: Breakdown by reaction such as dissolution or oxidation; lichen acids cause it while the category stays chemical.
entries.definitionCN: 由溶解、氧化一类反应造成的分解；地衣酸可造成它，而类别仍属化学风化。

entries.definition: The removal of coastal or submarine rock by boring and grazing organisms, including the transport of the debris.
entries.definitionCN: 钻孔与刮食生物把海岸或海底岩石移除，并包括碎屑的搬运。

entries.definition: A shorter form used in some journals for the same idea; the full phrase is standard in teaching.
entries.definitionCN: 部分期刊使用的较短形式，含义相同；教学中仍以完整短语为标准。

entries.definition: The formation of soil from rock and organic matter; it follows weathering but is a different process.
entries.definitionCN: 由岩石与有机物形成土壤的过程；它发生在风化之后，但属于另一过程。

entries.definition: The breakdown of dead organic matter by microbes; it is not the breakdown of rock.
entries.definitionCN: 微生物把死的有机物分解；对象并不是岩石。

entries.definition: The binding of metal ions by organic molecules, one way organisms pull minerals out of rock.
entries.definitionCN: 有机分子结合金属离子，是生物把矿物从岩石中取出的方式之一。

entries.definition: The specific widening of cracks by growing roots, the simplest example of this category.
entries.definitionCN: 生长的根把裂缝撑宽的具体过程，是本类别中最简单的例子。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real Greek life word, real organisms and real paired categories.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的希腊「生命」词、真实生物与真实的成对类别。

normal.en: Bio means life and logos means study, so biological simply points to living agents.
normal.cn: bio 是生命，logos 是研究，因此 biological 只是指向有生命的施力者。

normal.en: Two mechanisms sit inside one label: roots push, lichens dissolve.
normal.cn: 一个标签里有两种机制：根在推，地衣在溶。

normal.en: Lichen on bare lava is the textbook opening scene of soil formation.
normal.cn: 裸熔岩上的地衣是教科书里土壤形成的第一幕。

normal.en: Boring clams and grazing fish show the same word working on the coast.
normal.cn: 钻孔蛤与刮食鱼类说明这个词在海岸同样适用。

normal.en: The pair to remember is biological weathering versus bioerosion: decay in place against removal.
normal.cn: 要记住的一对是生物风化与生物侵蚀：原地分解对搬运移除。

abstract.en: Picture a lichen spreading like a slow grey stain that eats the stone under it.
abstract.cn: 想象地衣像一块慢慢扩大的灰斑，把下面的石头吃掉。

abstract.en: Picture a root feeling its way into a hairline crack and then thickening until the crack opens.
abstract.cn: 想象一条根摸索着钻进发丝般的裂缝，然后变粗直到裂缝张开。

abstract.en: Picture a shoreline where every hole in the rock was drilled by something alive.
abstract.cn: 想象一片海岸，岩石上每个孔都是活物钻出来的。

examples.en: Biological weathering by lichen is often the first sign that rock is breaking down.
examples.cn: 地衣造成的生物风化往往是岩石开始分解的第一个迹象。

examples.en: Tree roots cause biological weathering along the whole cliff edge.
examples.cn: 树根沿着整条崖边造成生物风化。

examples.en: The paper compares biological weathering with frost action at the same site.
examples.cn: 这篇论文比较了同一地点上的生物风化与冻融作用。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「生物 + 风化」——根在撑、地衣在蚀、动物在刨，全是活物在拆石头

root: biological（希腊 bios「生命」+ logos「研究」，经法语 biologie，加拉丁 -alis）+ weathering（古英语 weder「天气」加 -ing）；字面「由生命造成风化」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from the umbrella label to roots, lichens, animals, microbes, plant swelling, carved stone, and finally the sea.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从总标签走到根系、地衣、动物、微生物、植物胀缩、雕石，最后到海洋。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: lichen and roots working on bare rock.
core.cn: 核心意象：地衣与根须在裸岩上作业。

branches.en: THE LABEL: it names who acts, so the mechanism may be either force or reaction.
branches.cn: 标签：它命名谁在施力，因此机制可以是力，也可以是反应。

branches.en: PRESSURE: roots push and swell, both acting like small wedges.
branches.cn: 压力：根会推也会胀，都像小楔子。

branches.en: ACIDS: lichens and microbes dissolve minerals with what they release.
branches.cn: 酸：地衣与微生物用分泌物溶解矿物。

branches.en: DIGGING: animals break the crust and let water and air in.
branches.cn: 挖掘：动物破坏结皮，让水与空气进入。

branches.en: TWO SETTINGS: carved monuments lose their inscriptions, and coasts lose their rock.
branches.cn: 两个场景：雕石失去铭文，海岸失去岩石。

intro.en: Biological weathering is built from bio- plus -logical, then weathering from weather plus -ing.
intro.cn: biological weathering 由 bio- 加 -logical 构成前一词，再由 weather 加 -ing 构成后一词。

latinIntro.en: Both stems are Greek and the adjective ending is Latin -alis; Latin has no inherited form of the compound itself, so the entries below record only the ending and the Greek pieces.
latinIntro.cn: 两个词干都来自希腊语，形容词词尾为拉丁 -alis；拉丁语没有这个复合词本身的祖传形式，因此下面的词条只记录词尾与希腊构件。

items.example: Biology and biosphere both begin with the same element.
items.exampleCN: biology 与 biosphere 都以同一成分开头。

items.example: The ending -logy in geology keeps this sense.
items.exampleCN: geology 中的 -logy 保留了这一含义。

items.meaning: relating to a field of study
items.meaningCN: 与某一研究领域有关的
items.example: Biological and geological share the same ending.
items.exampleCN: biological 与 geological 共用同一词尾。

items.example: Biology explains how lichens colonise bare rock.
items.exampleCN: 生物学解释了地衣如何占据裸岩。

items.meaning: relating to life or living things
items.example: Biological agents break rock in several ways.
items.exampleCN: 生物媒介以多种方式破坏岩石。

items.meaning: from a biological point of view
items.example: The crust is biologically active even in winter.
items.exampleCN: 这层结皮即使在冬天也有生物活动。

items.example: The outcrop weathered slowly under the moss.
items.exampleCN: 苔藓之下的露头缓慢风化。

items.example: Weathering is the process, not the broken stone.
items.exampleCN: weathering 是过程，而不是碎掉的石头。

items.example: Bioerosion differs from weathering because the debris is carried off.
items.exampleCN: 生物侵蚀与风化的区别在于碎屑被搬走。

latinEntries.example: The -ical of biological rests on this Latin ending.
latinEntries.exampleCN: biological 的 -ical 建立在这个拉丁词尾上。

definition_zh: 缓和；减轻；平息；满足
definition_en: to make an unpleasant feeling less intense, or to satisfy a desire
core_image: 一只手轻按波涛，水面渐渐归于平静
scene: 暴雨过后洪水未退，堤上一夜未眠的人们终于听到水声低了下去。 Officials worked through the night to assuage the flood fears of the town.
sceneCN: 这里 assuage 是「缓和、平息」（第 1 个义项：减轻强烈的情绪）；句意为官员们连夜工作以平息镇民对洪水的恐惧。

pos.zh: 缓和；减轻（情绪、痛苦）
平息；满足（欲望、饥渴）

derivatives.zh: 由动词加名词后缀构成，义为「缓和；减轻」
同根形容词，义为「温和的；圆滑的」

senses.title: To ease a painful feeling
senses.definition: to make grief, fear, or pain less intense
senses.definitionCN: 使悲伤、恐惧或痛苦变得不那么强烈
senses.example: A warm meal can assuage sorrow for a while.
senses.exampleCN: 一顿热饭能暂时抚慰悲伤。
senses.why: Latin suavis meant sweet; sweetening a harsh feeling softens it.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 suavis 意为甜；给苦涩的情绪加点甜，它就缓和了。

senses.title: To satisfy a desire
senses.definition: to fulfil a craving such as hunger or curiosity
senses.definitionCN: 满足如饥饿、好奇之类的渴求
senses.example: Nothing could assuage his hunger for news.
senses.exampleCN: 什么都满足不了他对消息的渴求。
senses.why: A craving is an inner turbulence; satisfying it calms the surge.
senses.whyCN: 渴求是内心的翻腾；满足它便平息了这股涌动。

intro.en: Assuage comes from Old French asuagier, from Vulgar Latin *assuaviare, to sweeten, from Latin suavis.
intro.cn: assuage 源自古法语 asuagier，出自通俗拉丁语 *assuaviare（使变甜），词根为拉丁语 suavis（甜的）。

items.en: The root *swād- meant sweet.
items.cn: 词根 *swād- 意为甜。

items.en: Suavis meant sweet, pleasant.
items.cn: 拉丁语 suavis 意为甜的、令人愉快的。

items.en: Assuaviare meant to make sweet, hence to soften.
items.cn: 通俗拉丁语 assuaviare 意为使变甜，进而引申为使缓和。

items.en: Asuagier meant to calm or appease.
items.cn: 古法语 asuagier 意为使平静、安抚。

items.en: English adopted assuage in the fourteenth century.
items.cn: 十四世纪英语借入 assuage。

note.en: Assuage sweetens turmoil: the same root gives suave its smooth charm.
note.cn: assuage 给纷扰加糖：同根的 suave 也带着温和顺滑。

entries.definition: smoothly agreeable in manner
entries.definitionCN: 温文尔雅的（同根形容词）

entries.definition: the act of persuading
entries.definitionCN: 说服（同根名词）

entries.definition: to win over by talking
entries.definitionCN: 说服（同根）

entries.definition: similar opening letters, opposite meaning, different root
entries.definitionCN: 袭击（开头形似，意义相反，词源不同）

entries.definition: English cousin of the sweet root
entries.definitionCN: 甜的（同词根的英语表亲）

entries.definition: to soften someone's anger
entries.definitionCN: 抚慰；使息怒

entries.definition: to pacify by giving in
entries.definitionCN: 安抚；绥靖

entries.definition: to make less severe
entries.definitionCN: 减轻；缓解

entries.definition: to lay to rest a fear or doubt
entries.definitionCN: 平息；消除

entries.definition: to calm by pleasing
entries.definitionCN: 安抚

normalIntro.en: As + suage: think a-swaging, like a wave being smoothed flat.
normalIntro.cn: 把 assuage 想成 a-swage：像把一块铁敲平，把情绪熨平。

normal.en: suavis means sweet, the root of the word.
normal.cn: 词根 suavis 意为甜。

normal.en: sweeten a feeling to soften it.
normal.cn: 给情绪加甜即是软化。

normal.en: suave shares the same sweet root.
normal.cn: suave 同出甜的词根。

normal.en: common objects are fears and guilt.
normal.cn: 常见宾语是恐惧与内疚。

normal.en: it can also mean satisfy a craving.
normal.cn: 它也可表示满足渴求。

abstract.en: Picture honey stirred into bitter tea.
abstract.cn: 想象蜂蜜搅进苦茶。

abstract.en: See a storm easing into a drizzle.
abstract.cn: 看见暴风雨缓和成细雨。

abstract.en: Feel a clenched fist slowly opening.
abstract.cn: 体会紧握的拳头缓缓松开。

examples.en: The envoy's words assuaged the crowd's anger.
examples.cn: 特使的话平息了人群的怒火。

examples.en: He ate quickly to assuage his hunger.
examples.cn: 他狼吞虎咽以解饥饿。

examples.en: Nothing could assuage her grief that winter.
examples.cn: 那年冬天什么都抚不平她的悲伤。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「额斯为奇」——额视此物为奇甜之药，苦痛得解即 assuage。

root: 拉丁语 suavis（甜的）→ 通俗拉丁语 *assuaviare（使变甜）→ 古法语 asuagier（安抚）→ 英语 assuage（缓和；平息）。

sensesIntro.en: Sweetening a turmoil eases both raw feelings and inner cravings.
sensesIntro.cn: 给纷扰加甜，既抚平情绪，也喂饱欲求。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: honey poured onto a storm
core.cn: 核心意象：往风暴上浇蜂蜜

branches.en: easing grief or fear
branches.cn: 抚平悲伤或恐惧

branches.en: feeding a craving
branches.cn: 满足渴求

branches.en: the sweet root at work
branches.cn: 甜的词根在起作用

branches.en: gentle pacifying of anger
branches.cn: 温和地平息怒气

branches.en: quieting an inner surge
branches.cn: 平息内心的涌动

intro.en: The sweet root links soothing with pleasing, from taste to temper.
intro.cn: 甜的词根把抚慰与愉悦相连，从味觉到心绪。

latinIntro.en: Latin suavis, sweet, anchors the assuage family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 suavis（甜）是 assuage 词族的锚点。

definition_zh: 血管
definition_en: a tube in the body through which blood flows, such as an artery, vein or capillary
core_image: 体内一条细管，管壁内血液单向流动
scene: 这里指「血管」。 A blocked blood vessel in the brain can cause a stroke.
sceneCN: 这里 blood vessel 指「血管」（第 1 个义项：血液在体内流动的管道总称）；句意：脑内一条血管堵塞可能引发中风。图中可辨识物件：脑血管、血栓、脑部扫描、导管。

pos.zh: 血管（动脉、静脉与毛细血管的总称；可数）

senses.title: Any vessel carrying blood
senses.titleCN: 血管：运送血液的管道总称
senses.definition: a tube of any size through which blood is carried around the body
senses.definitionCN: 体内任何尺寸、用来运送血液的管道
senses.example: Blood vessels branch smaller and smaller as they reach the tissue.
senses.exampleCN: 血管到达组织时越分越细。
senses.why: The compound simply names the container and its content: a vessel for blood.
senses.whyCN: 这个复合词只是命名容器及其内容：装血的管子。

senses.title: An artery
senses.titleCN: 动脉：把血从心脏送出的血管
senses.definition: specifically, a vessel that carries blood away from the heart
senses.definitionCN: 特指把血液从心脏送出的血管
senses.example: The aorta is the largest blood vessel in the body.
senses.exampleCN: 主动脉是体内最大的血管。
senses.why: Anatomy divides the general word by direction of flow, and arteries are one half of that division.
senses.whyCN: 解剖学按血流方向划分这个通称，动脉是这一划分的一半。

senses.title: A vein
senses.titleCN: 静脉：把血送回心脏的血管
senses.definition: specifically, a vessel that carries blood back toward the heart
senses.definitionCN: 特指把血液送回心脏的血管
senses.example: A cut vein bleeds steadily rather than spurting.
senses.exampleCN: 静脉被割破后是持续渗血，而不是喷射。
senses.why: The return route is named by the same general term with a different qualifier.
senses.whyCN: 回流路径用同一个通称加不同限定来命名。

senses.title: A capillary
senses.titleCN: 毛细血管：气体与养分交换处
senses.definition: the smallest blood vessel, where exchange with tissue fluid takes place
senses.definitionCN: 最小的血管，与组织液进行物质交换的地方
senses.example: Oxygen crosses the wall of a capillary into the tissue.
senses.exampleCN: 氧气穿过毛细血管壁进入组织。
senses.why: The compound covers the finest branches too, where the tube becomes a permeable wall.
senses.whyCN: 这个通称也涵盖最细的分支，此时管道变成一层可渗透的壁。

senses.title: The vessel wall
senses.titleCN: 血管壁：管壁结构与弹性
senses.definition: the layered wall of a vessel, whose muscle and lining control flow
senses.definitionCN: 血管的分层管壁，其肌肉与内膜控制流动
senses.example: Cholesterol builds up inside a blood vessel wall.
senses.exampleCN: 胆固醇在血管壁内堆积。
senses.why: The physical tube has its own anatomy, so the phrase can name the wall rather than the lumen.
senses.whyCN: 这条实体管道自有解剖结构，因此这个短语也可指管壁而非管腔。

senses.title: Diseased vessel
senses.titleCN: 病变血管：堵塞、破裂或变窄
senses.definition: a vessel affected by blockage, rupture, inflammation or abnormal widening
senses.definitionCN: 受堵塞、破裂、炎症或异常扩张影响的血管
senses.example: A blocked blood vessel in the brain can cause a stroke.
senses.exampleCN: 脑内一条血管堵塞可能引发中风。
senses.why: Clinical writing uses the phrase as the site of pathology, not just as normal anatomy.
senses.whyCN: 临床写作把这个短语当作病变部位，而不只是正常解剖。

senses.title: The vessel network
senses.titleCN: 血管网络：器官内的整体分布
senses.definition: the whole arrangement of vessels supplying an organ or region
senses.definitionCN: 供应某个器官或区域的全部血管分布
senses.example: The liver has a dense blood vessel network.
senses.exampleCN: 肝脏有密集的血管网络。
senses.why: The count noun extends to the collective pattern, a shift from one tube to the system.
senses.whyCN: 可数名词扩展到整体格局，从一根管子转到整个系统。

senses.title: Vessel imaging
senses.titleCN: 血管成像：造影与超声检查
senses.definition: in medicine, the object visualized by angiography or ultrasound
senses.definitionCN: 医学中经血管造影或超声显像的对象
senses.example: The scan showed a narrow blood vessel near the heart.
senses.exampleCN: 扫描显示心脏附近有一条狭窄的血管。
senses.why: Radiology needed the phrase as the object of the image, because with contrast the vessel itself becomes visible.
senses.whyCN: 放射学需要这个短语作为成像的对象，因为使用造影剂后血管本身变得可见。

senses.title: New vessel growth
senses.titleCN: 血管新生：组织长出新血管
senses.definition: the formation of new vessels, as in healing, tumour growth or exercise adaptation
senses.definitionCN: 新血管的形成，见于愈合、肿瘤生长或运动适应
senses.example: Tumours release signals that trigger new blood vessel growth.
senses.exampleCN: 肿瘤释放信号，触发新血管生长。
senses.why: Research on angiogenesis made the phrase a target of drugs that starve tumours.
senses.whyCN: 血管生成研究使这个短语成为「饿死肿瘤」药物的靶点。

intro.en: Blood vessel is a native English compound: blood from Old English blod, vessel from Old French vaissel, ultimately Latin vascellum 'small container'. The dates below are approximate.
intro.cn: blood vessel 是英语本族复合词：blood 出自古英语 blod，vessel 经古法语 vaissel 上溯拉丁 vascellum「小容器」。以下年代均为约数。

items.en: Blod names blood and belongs to the native Germanic vocabulary; its deeper Indo-European connections are reconstructed, not recorded.
items.cn: blod 指血，属本族日耳曼词汇；其更深的印欧语联系属重构，并无记录。

items.en: Vas 'container' had the diminutive vascellum or vasculum 'small vessel', which passed through Old French vaissel into English vessel.
items.cn: vas「容器」的指小形式 vascellum 或 vasculum 意为「小容器」，经古法语 vaissel 进入英语 vessel。

items.en: The compound blood vessel is recorded in the fourteenth century, when anatomy needed a plain term for the tubes carrying blood.
items.cn: blood vessel 这一复合词记录于 14 世纪，当时解剖学需要为运血的管道找一个平实说法。

items.en: The seventeenth-century discovery of the circulation gave the phrase a fixed place in physiology, dividing vessels by direction of flow.
items.cn: 17 世纪发现血液循环，使这个短语在生理学中固定下来，并按血流方向划分血管。

items.en: Twentieth-century surgery and cancer research added phrases such as blood vessel formation and blood vessel wall.
items.cn: 20 世纪的外科学与癌症研究加入了 blood vessel formation、blood vessel wall 等说法。

items.en: Source uncertainty: the exact first citation is uncertain, and the deeper origin of both blod and vas is reconstructed rather than recorded.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代与更深词根）：最早书证年代存疑；blod 与 vas 的更深来源均属重构，而非有记录的实际词。

note.en: The first group holds the specific vessel types and the easily confused near-forms; the second holds broader terms for the vessel system.
note.cn: 第一组是具体的血管类型与易混近形词；第二组是血管系统的上位说法。

entries.definition: The blood flowing through the vessels; it names the content, while blood vessel names the container.
entries.definitionCN: 指在血管中流动的血液，命名内容物；blood vessel 命名容器。

entries.definition: A vessel carrying blood away from the heart; it is a type of blood vessel.
entries.definitionCN: 把血从心脏送出的血管，是血管的一种。

entries.definition: A vessel carrying blood back to the heart; the other main type of blood vessel.
entries.definitionCN: 把血送回心脏的血管，是血管的另一主要类型。

entries.definition: The smallest vessel, where exchange with tissue occurs.
entries.definitionCN: 最小的血管，与组织进行物质交换。

entries.definition: The collection of vessels in an organ or body; it is collective, while a blood vessel is countable.
entries.definitionCN: 某个器官或全身的血管集合，是集合名词；blood vessel 则可数。

entries.definition: The whole set of vessels taken as an anatomical system.
entries.definitionCN: 把全部血管视为一个解剖系统。

entries.definition: A small branch of an artery, too large to be a capillary.
entries.definitionCN: 动脉的小分支，比毛细血管大。

entries.definition: A small vein that collects blood from capillaries.
entries.definitionCN: 从毛细血管收集血液的小静脉。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: blood + vessel: a container for blood, exactly as the two words say.
normal.cn: blood + vessel：装血的容器，两个词字面就说清了。

normal.en: vessel comes from Latin vascellum 'small container', the same root as vascular.
normal.cn: vessel 出自拉丁 vascellum「小容器」，与 vascular 同根。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the clinic: blocked blood vessel, blood vessel wall, burst blood vessel.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出临床语境：堵塞的血管、血管壁、血管破裂。

normal.en: The three types are artery, vein and capillary.
normal.cn: 三种类型是动脉、静脉与毛细血管。

normal.en: bloodstream is the contents; blood vessel is the tube.
normal.cn: bloodstream 是内容物，blood vessel 是管道。

abstract.en: Picture a branching river system inside the body, with the heart as its source.
abstract.cn: 想象体内一套分叉的河流系统，心脏是源头。

abstract.en: Picture a pipe narrowing until its wall becomes thin enough for oxygen to slip through.
abstract.cn: 想象管道不断变窄，管壁薄到氧气能穿过去。

abstract.en: Picture a scan lighting up a single narrow channel beside a beating heart.
abstract.cn: 想象扫描图上，跳动的心脏旁亮起一条狭窄通道。

examples.en: Damaged blood vessels in the retina can blur vision.
examples.cn: 视网膜受损的血管会使视力模糊。

examples.en: Exercise improves blood vessel function within a few weeks.
examples.cn: 运动在几周内就能改善血管功能。

examples.en: The surgeon grafted a healthy blood vessel onto the blocked artery.
examples.cn: 外科医生把一段健康血管接到堵塞的动脉上。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「blood 血 + vessel 容器」——装血的容器 → blood vessel 血管

root: 古英语 blod「血」+ 古法语 vaissel（拉丁 vascellum「小容器」）→ 英语复合词 blood vessel。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses follow one tube: blood runs through it, and that tube can be classified by direction, narrowed to the smallest branch, examined in its wall, diseased, counted as a network, imaged, or newly grown.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项沿同一根管子展开：血液流过它，而这根管子可按方向分类、缩小到最细分支、细看管壁、成为病灶、作为网络计数、被成像，或新长出来。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a tube inside the body with blood moving along it.
core.cn: 核心意象：体内一根管子，血液沿它流动。

branches.en: THREE NAMED FORMS: artery, vein and capillary are the specialised types of tube.
branches.cn: 三种专名：动脉、静脉与毛细血管是管道的专门形态。

branches.en: THE PHYSICAL TUBE: the wall that can thicken, and the vessel that can block or burst.
branches.cn: 实体管道：可以增厚的管壁，以及会堵塞或破裂的血管。

branches.en: THE NETWORK AND THE IMAGE: many tubes taken together, and the same tubes seen on a scan.
branches.cn: 网络与影像：多根管子合起来看，以及同一批管子在扫描图上的样子。

branches.en: NEW TUBES: healing and tumours both build vessels, which makes the phrase a drug target.
branches.cn: 新管子：愈合与肿瘤都会造血管，这使该短语成为药物靶点。

branches.en: THE CONTAINER LOGIC: vessel means container, so the compound never means the blood itself.
branches.cn: 容器逻辑：vessel 意为容器，因此这个复合词从不指血液本身。

intro.en: Blood vessel is a native compound of a Germanic word for blood and a Latin-derived word for container.
intro.cn: blood vessel 是「日耳曼语的血」与「拉丁来源的容器」构成的本族复合词。

latinIntro.en: Latin vas 'container' gives vascellum, vasculum, vascular and vasculature; English vessel arrived through Old French vaissel.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 vas「容器」产生 vascellum、vasculum、vascular、vasculature；英语 vessel 经古法语 vaissel 进入。

items.example: The clot blocked a small blood vessel.
items.exampleCN: 血栓堵住了一条小血管。

items.example: The skin has a rich vasculature.
items.exampleCN: 皮肤有丰富的血管网络。
移植物在几周内形成了血管。
血管形成不良会延缓愈合。
血管生成供养不断长大的肿瘤。

items.meaning: a vessel carrying blood away from the heart
items.meaningCN: 把血从心脏送出的血管
items.example: The carotid artery supplies the brain.

items.meaning: a vessel carrying blood back to the heart
items.example: The vein was used for the drip.

definition_zh: 本质上；内在地；就其本身而言
definition_en: by the nature of the thing itself, considered apart from its use or setting
core_image: 一枚宝石在暗室里自己发亮，不靠外面的灯
scene: 老师提醒学生，读诗不该只为了考试得分。 Reading poetry is intrinsically rewarding, even without an exam.
sceneCN: 这里指活动本身带来的价值（第 3 个义项：为自身之故而被重视）；句意为读诗本身就有回报，即使没有考试。

pos.zh: 本质上；内在地；就其本身而言

senses.title: In itself
senses.definition: by the nature of the thing itself, apart from its use or setting
senses.definitionCN: 按事物本身的性质，撇开用途与处境
senses.example: The claim is intrinsically interesting, whatever its practical value.
senses.exampleCN: 无论实际价值如何，这个说法本身就有趣。
senses.why: The word isolates the thing from external purposes and asks what it is like on its own.
senses.whyCN: 这个词把事物从外部目的中隔出来，问它单独来看是什么样。

senses.title: As an essential property
senses.definition: of a quality that belongs to the thing and cannot be removed
senses.definitionCN: 指属于该事物、无法去掉的性质
senses.example: Diamond is intrinsically hard, though a sharp blow can still shatter it.
senses.exampleCN: 钻石本身是硬的，尽管一记猛击仍能把它打碎。
senses.why: Unlike inherent, which stresses inseparable belonging, this word stresses the property viewed in itself.
senses.whyCN: 与强调「不可分离地属于」的固有一词不同，这个词强调的是把性质放在它自身来看。

senses.title: For its own sake
senses.definition: of an activity valued for itself rather than for a reward
senses.definitionCN: 指某项活动因自身而被重视，而非为了回报
senses.example: They study the language intrinsically, not for a certificate.
senses.exampleCN: 他们学这门语言是出于本身兴趣，而不是为了证书。
senses.why: The contrast with external reward is the heart of the word's motivational use.
senses.whyCN: 与外部回报的对照，正是这个词在动机语境中的核心。

senses.title: Intrinsically motivated
senses.definition: in psychology, describing drive that comes from interest or enjoyment
senses.definitionCN: 在心理学中指来自兴趣或愉悦的驱动力
senses.example: Intrinsically motivated students keep working after the task is over.
senses.exampleCN: 受内在动机驱动的学生在任务结束后仍继续钻研。
senses.why: The field fixed the term to separate interest-driven effort from reward-driven effort.
senses.whyCN: 心理学固定了这一术语，用来把兴趣驱动的努力与奖励驱动的努力分开。

senses.title: Intrinsically linked
senses.definition: used of things connected by their very definitions
senses.definitionCN: 指按定义本身就连在一起的事物
senses.example: Meaning is intrinsically linked to use in a community.
senses.exampleCN: 意义与社群中的使用本质上相联系。
senses.why: The fixed pattern says the link is not accidental but part of what the things are.
senses.whyCN: 这一固定搭配说明联系并非偶然，而是事物本身的一部分。

senses.title: Intrinsically valuable
senses.definition: in ethics, valuable without reference to usefulness
senses.definitionCN: 在伦理学中，指不涉及用途即具有价值
senses.example: The wetland is intrinsically valuable, beyond the fish it yields.
senses.exampleCN: 这片湿地本身就有价值，并不只在于它产出的鱼。
senses.why: Moral philosophy uses the word to resist pricing everything by its output.
senses.whyCN: 道德哲学用它抵制把一切按产出定价的做法。

senses.title: Intrinsically unstable
senses.definition: of a system, unstable because of its own structure
senses.definitionCN: 指系统因自身结构而不稳定
senses.example: The reaction is intrinsically unstable and needs constant cooling.
senses.exampleCN: 这个反应本身就不稳定，需要持续冷却。
senses.why: Engineering uses the word for properties that cannot be fixed by better control alone.
senses.whyCN: 工程领域用它指单靠更好的控制也无法解决的性质。

senses.title: Intrinsically safe
senses.titleCN: 本安型的技术固定称法
senses.definition: of equipment, designed so that it cannot release enough energy to ignite a hazard
senses.definitionCN: 指设备经设计后无法释放足以点燃危险的能量
senses.example: Intrinsically safe sensors are used in fuel storage areas.
senses.exampleCN: 本安型传感器被用于燃料储存区。
senses.why: The phrase became a fixed technical label, where the word marks safety by design rather than by added protection.
senses.whyCN: 这一说法成为固定的技术标签，词在这里指「靠设计本身安全」，而不是外加防护。

intro.en: Intrinsically comes from the Latin adverb meaning inwardly, later an adjective, plus the English adverb suffix. The direct source is clear; only the first English date is approximate.
intro.cn: 这个副词来自拉丁语「向内、在内部」的副词，后来转为形容词，再加英语副词后缀。直接来源清楚，只有英语首见年代为约数。

items.en: The preposition intra means within.
items.cn: 介词意为「在……之内」。

items.en: The old adverb secus means beside, along or otherwise, and combines with intra.
items.cn: 古副词意为「在旁边、沿着」，与「在内」组合。

items.en: Latin intrinsecus means inwardly or on the inside, first as an adverb.
items.cn: 拉丁语副词意为「向内、在内部」。

items.en: Medieval Latin uses intrinsecus as an adjective meaning inner or inherent.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语把它用作形容词，意为「内部的、固有的」。

items.en: English intrinsic appears in the seventeenth century; the exact first date is approximate.
items.cn: 英语形容词在十七世纪出现，确切首见年代为约数。

items.en: The adverb adds the usual suffix and grows strong in philosophy, psychology and engineering.
items.cn: 副词加常见后缀，并在哲学、心理学与工程领域壮大。

note.en: The first group shares the Latin inside-stem, including its opposite; the second group contrasts value or quality viewed in itself with qualities inseparable from a thing.
note.cn: 第一组共享拉丁语「内部」词干，包括其反义形式；第二组对照「就本身而言」的价值或性质与「不可分离」的属性。

entries.definition: Belonging to the nature of a thing; the adjective behind the adverb.
entries.definitionCN: 属于事物本性的；副词的形容词基形。

entries.definition: An older variant of the adjective, now rare.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词的旧式变体，现已少用。

entries.definition: From outside, by external circumstances rather than inner nature.
entries.definitionCN: 从外部、由外在处境而非内在本性决定地。

entries.definition: As an inseparable part of a thing's nature; close, but stressing belonging more than self-view.
entries.definitionCN: 作为事物本性中不可分离的部分；意思接近，但更强调「属于」而非「就本身看」。

entries.definition: From birth or from the earliest nature, often of living things.
entries.definitionCN: 与生俱来地，多用于生物。

entries.definition: In essential respects, setting aside what is secondary.
entries.definitionCN: 在本质方面，撇开次要因素。

entries.definition: Because of the character a thing has.
entries.definitionCN: 由于事物本身的特性。

entries.definition: At the deepest or most basic level.
entries.definitionCN: 在最深层、最基础的层面上。

entries.definition: Considered apart from its relations or uses.
entries.definitionCN: 撇开其关系或用途来考虑。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real inside-stem and the real contrast between value in itself and external reward.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的「内部」词根，并对照「自身价值」与「外部回报」。

normal.en: The root says within, so the word asks what a thing is like once you step inside it.
normal.cn: 词根说的是「在内」，所以这个词问的是：走进事物内部后它是什么样。

normal.en: Intrinsic value is what remains when the price tag is removed.
normal.cn: 内在价值就是撕掉价签之后仍然剩下的东西。

normal.en: In psychology it marks effort that continues after the reward is gone.
normal.cn: 在心理学里，它标记奖励消失后仍继续的努力。

normal.en: Intrinsically safe is a technical badge, not a compliment.
normal.cn: 「本安型」是技术标签，不是一句称赞。

normal.en: The word often appears with linked, valuable or motivated, and those partners fix its meaning.
normal.cn: 这个词常与「相联系」「有价值的」「有动机的」搭配，搭档固定了它的意思。

abstract.en: What is intrinsic needs no audience; it is already complete in private.
abstract.cn: 内在之物不需要观众，它在私下里已经完整。

abstract.en: Calling something intrinsically valuable is refusing to let the market finish the sentence.
abstract.cn: 说某物本身有价值，就是拒绝让市场把后半句说完。

abstract.en: The view from inside is not the whole truth, but it is the one the word insists on.
abstract.cn: 内部的视角不是全部真相，却是这个词坚持要看的那一面。

examples.en: The problem is intrinsically difficult, not merely badly explained.
examples.cn: 这个问题本身就有难度，不只是讲解得不好。

examples.en: They value the practice intrinsically, not for the medals it brings.
examples.cn: 他们重视这项练习本身，而不是它能带来的奖牌。

examples.en: The system is intrinsically unstable, so outside control cannot fix it.
examples.cn: 这个系统本身不稳定，外部控制无法解决。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「因吹恩济克」——往里看，性质长在事物内部

root: 拉丁语介词「在内」与古副词「在旁边」合成副词「向内、在内部」，中世纪拉丁语转为形容词「内部的、固有的」；英语借入形容词后加副词后缀。直接来源清楚，只有英语首见年代为约数。

sensesIntro.en: The eight senses separate self-consideration, essential property, value for its own sake, intrinsic motivation, definitional linking, moral value, structural instability and the fixed safety label.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项分开处理就本身而言、本质属性、为自身之故、内在动机、定义性联系、道德价值、结构性不稳定，以及固定的本安型标签。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a gem that glows in a dark room without any lamp outside.
core.cn: 核心意象：一枚宝石在暗室里自己发亮，不靠外面的灯。

branches.en: THE THING ALONE: considered apart from use and setting.
branches.cn: 单独的事物：撇开用途与处境来看。

branches.en: THE PROPERTY: a quality that belongs to what the thing is.
branches.cn: 属性：属于事物之所以为该物的性质。

branches.en: THE INNER DRIVE: value for its own sake and interest-driven effort.
branches.cn: 内在驱动：为自身之故的价值与兴趣驱动的努力。

branches.en: THE GROUND OF VALUE: definitional linking and worth without usefulness.
branches.cn: 价值的根基：定义性联系与不靠用途的价值。

branches.en: THE BUILT-IN CONDITION: structural instability and the fixed safety label.
branches.cn: 内置状况：结构性不稳定与固定的安全标签。

intro.en: Intrinsically is a Latin within-prefix, an old alongside-word, an adjective layer and an English adverb suffix; the opposite is built with a different prefix.
intro.cn: 这个副词由拉丁语「在内」、古副词「在旁边」、形容词层与英语副词后缀构成；反义词则用另一个前缀构成。

latinIntro.en: The inner word and the alongside word combine into an adverb of inwardness, which later becomes an adjective.
latinIntro.cn: 表示「在内」的词与表示「在旁边」的词合成表「向内」的副词，后来又转为形容词。

items.example: The preposition places the whole word inside a boundary.
items.exampleCN: 这个介词把整个词放进一条边界之内。

items.example: The old adverb adds the idea of a side or flank.
items.exampleCN: 这个古副词加上「侧边、旁侧」的意思。

items.example: The compound first describes direction and then quality.
items.exampleCN: 这个合成词先描述方向，再描述性质。

items.example: The matching outward form supplies the modern opposite.
items.exampleCN: 对应的「向外」形式提供现代的反义词。

items.example: English shortens the Latin adverb into an adjective.
items.exampleCN: 英语把拉丁副词缩短成形容词。

items.example: The opposite keeps the same shape with a different prefix.
items.exampleCN: 反义词保持同一形状，只换前缀。

items.example: The suffix turns the Latin stem into an adjective.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把拉丁词干变成形容词。

items.example: The suffix turns the adjective into a manner adverb.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把形容词变成方式副词。

items.example: The rare noun names the quality the adverb describes.
items.exampleCN: 这个少见名词命名副词所描述的性质。

definition_zh: 大包；大捆；（古义）灾祸；悲痛
definition_en: a large bound bundle of goods such as hay or cotton; also, an archaic word for evil or sorrow
core_image: 田野尽头码得整整齐齐的方形草捆
scene: 拖拉机把最后一捆干草推上垛顶。 The crew loaded bales of cotton onto the flatbed.
sceneCN: 这里 bale 指「大包、大捆」（第 1 个义项：打包成捆的货物）；句意：工人们把一捆捆棉花装上平板车。

pos.zh: 大包；大捆；（废义）灾祸；悲伤
打包；捆扎

derivatives.zh: 有害的；凶恶的（出自古义 bale「灾祸」+ -ful）

senses.title: A large bound bundle
senses.definition: a large quantity of a compressible good pressed and tied into a block
senses.definitionCN: 可压缩货物被压实捆扎成的大块
senses.example: Hay bales dotted the field after harvest.
senses.exampleCN: 收割后，干草捆星星点点布满田野。
senses.why: The commercial root is Middle Dutch bale, a pack of goods.
senses.whyCN: 商业词根是中古荷兰语 bale「货包」。

senses.title: A standard trade unit
senses.definition: a fixed weight or measure of cotton, wool, or paper used in trade
senses.definitionCN: 棉花、羊毛、纸张等在贸易中固定的重量单位
senses.example: Cotton is quoted per bale on the exchange.
senses.exampleCN: 交易所以每包为单位报棉花价格。
senses.why: Trade standardized the bundle into a unit of account.
senses.whyCN: 贸易把草捆标准化为记账单位。

senses.title: To press and tie into bundles
senses.definition: to compress and bind a material into bales
senses.definitionCN: 把材料压实并捆成大包
senses.example: Volunteers baled cardboard for recycling.
senses.exampleCN: 志愿者把纸板打包回收。
senses.why: The noun made a verb of itself, as goods nouns do.
senses.whyCN: 货物名词自我动词化，一如常态。

senses.title: Bale out, to jump from a plane
senses.definition: in British use, to parachute from a disabled aircraft
senses.definitionCN: 英式用法，从失控飞机跳伞
senses.example: The pilot baled out at eight hundred feet.
senses.exampleCN: 飞行员在八百英尺高空跳伞。
senses.why: Distinct from bail out; British spelling keeps the e.
senses.whyCN: 与 bail out 有别；英式拼写保留 e。

senses.title: Archaic: evil or harm
senses.definition: in archaic English, mischief, sorrow, or destruction
senses.definitionCN: 古英语中指祸患、悲恸或毁灭
senses.example: The poet sang of woe and bale.
senses.exampleCN: 诗人吟咏哀恸与灾殃。
senses.why: A native Germanic word, unrelated to the bundle.
senses.whyCN: 这是本族日耳曼词，与「货包」毫无关系。

senses.title: Archaic: burning, as hell-fire
senses.definition: in old poetry, fire, especially the flames of hell
senses.definitionCN: 古诗中指火焰，尤指地狱之火
senses.example: Sermons painted the bale of the damned.
senses.exampleCN: 布道描绘受诅者的地狱之火。
senses.why: A second native homograph, from a word to burn.
senses.whyCN: 第二个同形本族词，源自「燃烧」一词。

senses.title: Baleful, the survival of old bale
senses.definition: the adjective baleful preserves the archaic sorrow-and-harm sense
senses.definitionCN: 形容词 baleful 保存了古义的「灾殃、伤害」
senses.example: A baleful stare stopped the argument.
senses.exampleCN: 一道凶狠的目光让争论戛然而止。
senses.why: The noun died, but its adjective lives on in daily use.
senses.whyCN: 名词已死，其形容词却活跃至今。

senses.title: Baled waste, the modern industry
senses.definition: compressed recyclables, from cardboard to scrap metal
senses.definitionCN: 从纸板到废金属的压块回收物
senses.example: The yard stacked baled aluminum by the ton.
senses.exampleCN: 回收场按吨堆放压块的铝料。
senses.why: The oldest commercial sense found a green second life.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的商业义在回收业获得新生。

intro.en: English has two bales: the bundle, from Middle Dutch bale or Old French bale, a pack for transport; and the sorrow, from Old English bealu, evil or destruction, cognate with the first element of the names Böðvarr and Baldwin in their Germanic forms.
intro.cn: 英语有两个 bale：「货包」出自中古荷兰语 bale 或古法语 bale，指运输货包；「灾殃」出自古英语 bealu「邪恶、毁灭」，与日耳曼人名中的 Baldwin 等词的首成分同源。

items.en: The sorrow-root is reconstructed as balu-, harm or destruction.
items.cn: 「灾殃」词根被重构为 balu-「伤害、毁灭」。

items.en: bealu meant evil, wickedness, or destruction, a strong poetic word.
items.cn: 古英语 bealu 指邪恶、残暴或毁灭，是强的诗歌用词。

items.en: The bundle-word crossed from Middle Dutch bale, a pack of merchandise.
items.cn: 「货包」一词由中古荷兰语 bale「商货包」传入。

items.en: The trading bale entered English by the fourteenth century with the wool trade.
items.cn: 14 世纪随羊毛贸易，商业 bale 进入英语。

items.en: The verb to bale is recorded from the sixteenth century.
items.cn: 动词 to bale 见于 16 世纪记载。

items.en: The sorrow-bale survives only in baleful; the bundle-bale thrives in farm and scrapyard.
items.cn: 「灾殃」义仅存于 baleful；「货包」义活跃于农场与回收场。

note.en: Group one gathers the homograph pair and the bail family; group two gathers bundle and doom words.
note.cn: 第一组收同形词对与 bail 词族；第二组收货包与厄运义场的词。

entries.definition: to scoop water, post bond, or (US) jump from a plane; the eternal spelling trap.
entries.definitionCN: 舀水、保释或（美）跳伞；与 bale 同音，永恒的拼写陷阱。

entries.definition: sinister and harmful; the living descendant of bealu.
entries.definitionCN: 凶恶有害的；bealu 的存世后裔。

entries.definition: ship's weighting cargo, from the same Low-German trading world.
entries.definitionCN: 船舶压舱物；出自同一低地德语商贸圈。

entries.definition: a loosely tied group of things.
entries.definitionCN: 松散捆扎的一包东西。

entries.definition: a bound bundle of grain stalks.
entries.definitionCN: 捆扎的谷物秆束。

entries.definition: a wrapped or boxed quantity for carrying.
entries.definitionCN: 便于携带的包装量。

entries.definition: deep sorrow; the modern cousin of old bale.
entries.definitionCN: 深重的悲哀；古义 bale 的现代近亲。

entries.definition: utter ruin, especially damnation.
entries.definitionCN: 彻底毁灭，尤指永罚；古义 bale 的近亲。

normalIntro.en: Two bales share one sound: the farmer's bundle and the poet's sorrow.
normalIntro.cn: 两个 bale 同音：农人的货包与诗人的哀愁。

normal.en: a bale of hay: the everyday phrase.
normal.cn: a bale of hay 是日常搭配。

normal.en: British bale out, American bail out, for parachutes.
normal.cn: 跳伞英式用 bale out，美式用 bail out。

normal.en: baleful comes from the other bale: evil, sorrow.
normal.cn: baleful 出自另一个 bale：邪恶、悲恸。

normal.en: Baler, the machine, doubles as an Australian town name.
normal.cn: 打捆机 baler 恰与澳大利亚地名 Baler 同拼。

normal.en: Spelling check: the bundle has the e, bale.
normal.cn: 拼写检查：货包义带 e，作 bale。

abstract.en: See twine bite into a golden cube.
abstract.cn: 看麻绳咬进金色的方块。

abstract.en: Old bale is the ash-word from the fire sermons.
abstract.cn: 古义 bale 是火刑布道里烧剩的灰词。

abstract.en: Hear the baling machine sigh at the end of the field.
abstract.cn: 听打捆机在田头的长叹。

examples.en: The loft held forty bales of straw.
examples.cn: 草棚里堆着四十捆麦秸。

examples.en: Mill workers baled the rags for shipment north.
examples.cn: 磨坊工人把破布打包北运。

examples.en: The chronicle speaks of fire and bale upon the town.
examples.cn: 编年史记载大火与灾殃降临城池。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「贝耦」——两捆贝壳用绳子耦在一起，就成了大包

root: 英语中有两个同形 bale：一为「货包」，14 世纪经中古荷兰语 bale 或古法语 bale 进入英语，与羊毛贸易相关；一为「灾殃、悲恸」，出自古英语 bealu「邪恶、毁灭」，词根可追溯至原始日耳曼语 balu-，另有一个表「火」的同源古词。今前者通行，后者仅存于形容词 baleful。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses split along the homograph seam: the farming and trading bundle on one side, and the archaic sorrow and fire on the other, with baleful as the living bridge.
sensesIntro.cn: 八义项沿同形词的裂缝分开：一边是农牧贸易的货包，另一边是古义的悲恸与烈火，baleful 则是存活的桥梁。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a compressed cube tied tight, and, underneath the word, an older flame.
core.cn: 核心意象：捆得紧紧的方块；而在词的底层，埋着一团更古老的火。

branches.en: THE FARM SIDE: hay, straw, and baled recyclables.
branches.cn: 农牧一面：干草、麦秸与压块回收物。

branches.en: THE TRADE SIDE: the bale as a unit of price.
branches.cn: 贸易一面：作为计价单位的包。

branches.en: THE AVIATION SIDE: bale out in British skies.
branches.cn: 航空一面：英国空军说的 bale out。

branches.en: THE ARCHAIC SIDE: sorrow surviving in baleful.
branches.cn: 古义一面：存于 baleful 中的悲恸。

branches.en: THE FIRE SIDE: hell-fire of the lost homograph.
branches.cn: 烈火一面：另一同形词的地狱之火。

intro.en: Neither bale takes affixes of its own; both are bare roots that borrowed English endings.
intro.cn: 两个 bale 本身都不带词缀，皆为裸词根，只借英语词尾。

latinIntro.en: No Latin here: one bale is Low-German trade speech, the other native Old English poetry.
latinIntro.cn: 与拉丁语无关：一个 bale 是低地德语的商贸语，另一个是古英语诗歌本族词。

definition_zh: 副官；（军队中的）人事参谋；鹳（一种鸟）
definition_en: a staff officer who helps a commander with administration; also a large stork-like bird
core_image: 站在长官身后的参谋，递文件、排班表样样在行
scene: 营部办公室里，军官把命令写好，交给身旁的助手去分发。 The colonel sent the orders out through his adjutant.
sceneCN: 这里 adjutant 是「副官」（第 1 个义项：协助长官处理行政事务的参谋军官）；句意为上校经副官把命令分发出去。

pos.zh: 副官；人事参谋
鹳（大鸟，鸟类名）

derivatives.zh: 由本词加名词后缀构成，义为「副官职务」
同根罕用词，义为「导水管；管口」

senses.title: A staff officer who assists
senses.definition: an officer who helps a commander with orders, records, and administration
senses.definitionCN: 协助指挥官处理命令、记录与行政的军官
senses.example: The colonel sent the orders out through his adjutant.
senses.exampleCN: 上校经副官把命令分发出去。
senses.why: Latin iuvare means 'to help'; the adjutant is the officer whose whole job is to help the commander.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 iuvare 意为「帮助」；adjutant 就是专门帮助指挥官的军官。

senses.title: A large stork-like bird
senses.definition: a tall Indian bird, so named as if the 'helper' of vultures at carcasses
senses.definitionCN: 印度的一种高大鸟类，因似「帮助」秃鹫拾余而得名
senses.example: The adjutant stalked the riverbank behind the feeding vultures.
senses.exampleCN: 副官鹳跟在进食的秃鹫后面沿河岸踱步。
senses.why: The bird was called the vulture's 'helper', picking up what the vultures leave.
senses.whyCN: 这种鸟被称为秃鹫的「帮手」，捡拾秃鹫吃剩的东西。

intro.en: Adjutant comes from Latin adjutare, 'to help', a frequentative of iuvare, 'to help'.
intro.cn: adjutant 来自拉丁语 adjutare（帮助），是 iuvare（帮助）的反复态。

items.en: The reconstructed root *yeu- is thought to mean 'to help'; it remains uncertain.
items.cn: 一般认为重构词根 *yeu- 意为「帮助」；此说尚存疑。

items.en: iuvare meant 'to help'; adjutare meant 'to help repeatedly'.
items.cn: iuvare 意为「帮助」；adjutare 意为「一再帮助」。

items.en: adjutans was the present participle, 'one who helps'.
items.cn: adjutans 是现在分词：「帮助者」。

items.en: English adjutant first named a military staff officer.
items.cn: 英语 adjutant 最初指军队参谋军官。

items.en: The military sense is standard; the bird name survives in natural history.
items.cn: 军义项是标准用法；鸟名留存在博物学中。

note.en: The first group gathers the iuvare family; the second gathers words for assisting roles.
note.cn: 第一组收 iuvare 词族；第二组收表示协助角色的词。

entries.definition: A rare technical word for a tube or nozzle.
entries.definitionCN: 罕用技术名词，义为「导水管、管口」。

entries.definition: The office or term of an adjutant.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「副官职务」。

entries.definition: A military helper of different Latin origin; spelling and meaning near.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「副官」；词源不同，拼写相近。

entries.definition: A personal officer assisting a general.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「随从副官」。

entries.definition: Any officer serving headquarters rather than the line.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「参谋军官」。

entries.definition: A general helper, the civilian cousin.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「助手」，是文职近亲。

normalIntro.en: The normal hooks use the help root iuvare and the headquarters scene; the abstract hooks picture papers passed behind the commander.
normalIntro.cn: 常规记忆点用「帮助」词根 iuvare 与司令部场景；抽象记忆点想象在指挥官身后传递文件。

normal.en: Adjutant is adjutare: the one who keeps helping.
normal.cn: adjutant 出自 adjutare：持续帮忙的人。

normal.en: Adjutant general is the senior staff title.
normal.cn: adjutant general 是高级参谋头衔。

normal.en: The bird name comes from playing the vulture's helper.
normal.cn: 鸟名来自它扮演秃鹫帮手。

normal.en: Aide is the French cousin with the same job.
normal.cn: aide 是干同样差事的法语近亲。

normal.en: The plural is simply adjutants.
normal.cn: 复数就是 adjutants。

abstract.en: Picture a desk where every paper passes through one hand.
abstract.cn: 想象每份文件都要经过一只手的办公桌。

abstract.en: Picture a second chair always beside the commander.
abstract.cn: 想象指挥官身旁永远摆着的第二把椅子。

abstract.en: Picture a bird trailing the clean-up crew.
abstract.cn: 想象跟在清洁队后面踱步的大鸟。

examples.en: The colonel sent the orders out through his adjutant.
examples.cn: 上校经副官把命令分发出去。

examples.en: The adjutant kept the regiment's records in perfect order.
examples.cn: 副官把团里的档案整理得井井有条。

examples.en: The adjutant stalked the riverbank behind the feeding vultures.
examples.cn: 副官鹳跟在进食的秃鹫后面沿河岸踱步。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「额久他特」——长官身边久待的特别帮手，就是副官。

root: 拉丁语 iuvare（帮助）→ adjutare（一再帮助）→ adjutans（帮助者）；核心义是「长在指挥官身边的帮助之手」

sensesIntro.en: The senses move from the officer who helps command, to the bird once called the vulture's helper.
sensesIntro.cn: 这些义项从协助指挥的军官，走到曾被称作秃鹫帮手的鸟。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the helping hand always beside the commander
core.cn: 核心意象：常伴指挥官左右的帮助之手

branches.en: The officer whose trade is assistance.
branches.cn: 以协助为本职的军官。

branches.en: The bird that 'helps' the vultures.
branches.cn: 「帮助」秃鹫的鸟。

branches.en: Both names rest on the Latin idea of helping.
branches.cn: 两个名称都立足拉丁语「帮助」的观念。

branches.en: Headquarters paperwork is this sense's daily work.
branches.cn: 司令部的文书是这一义项的日常。

branches.en: Natural history keeps this sense alive.
branches.cn: 博物学让这个义项留存。

intro.en: The word carries the help-root jut- with the agent ending -ant, and the family spreads into aid and auxiliary through related verbs.
intro.cn: 这个词带着「帮助」词根 jut- 与施动词尾 -ant，词族经相关动词延伸到 aid 与 auxiliary。

latinIntro.en: Latin iuvare and adjutare are the recorded ancestors.
latinIntro.cn: 记录在案的祖先是拉丁语 iuvare 与 adjutare。

definition_zh: 副业；业余爱好；消遣
definition_en: a hobby or minor occupation pursued alongside one's main work
core_image: 白天在诊室听诊，晚上在阁楼刻木版
scene: 钢笔律师放下公文包，取出刻刀。 Bookbinding became his avocation after retirement.
sceneCN: 这里 avocation 指「业余爱好」（第 1 个义项：主业之外的消遣）；句意：退休后，装订书成了他的业余爱好。

pos.zh: 副业；业余爱好；消遣

collocations.phrase: turn an avocation into a vocation

derivatives.zh: 职业；天职（同根反义对照词）

senses.title: A hobby beside one's work
senses.definition: an activity followed for pleasure in spare time, apart from the main job
senses.definitionCN: 业余时间出于兴趣从事的活动，非主业
senses.example: Her avocation was restoring old clocks.
senses.exampleCN: 她的业余爱好是修复老钟表。
senses.why: The Latin root avocare means to call away: the hobby calls you away from work.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根 avocare 意为「唤走」：爱好把你从正事上唤走。

senses.title: A minor occupation
senses.definition: a small secondary occupation, sometimes earning a little money
senses.definitionCN: 次要的营生，有时略有收入
senses.example: Beekeeping was a modest avocation that paid for itself.
senses.exampleCN: 养蜂是份小副业，勉强自给。
senses.why: Called-away time can still be work, only second-ranked.
senses.whyCN: 被唤走的时光也可以是劳作，只是排位居次。

senses.title: One's usual calling, in older use
senses.definition: in older English, a person's regular business or calling
senses.definitionCN: 旧式英语中指某人的常规营生
senses.example: The letter mentioned his avocation as a surveyor.
senses.exampleCN: 信中提到他做测量员的营生。
senses.why: Early usage sat closer to the Latin: whatever calls you, even the job.
senses.whyCN: 早期用法更贴近拉丁语：凡「呼唤你」的，包括职业本身。

senses.title: Distraction or diversion
senses.definition: something that diverts or relieves the mind from serious affairs
senses.definitionCN: 使心思从正务上得到消解与放松之物
senses.example: Gardening served the judge as a needed avocation.
senses.exampleCN: 园艺是法官不可或缺的调剂。
senses.why: The calling-away is the point: relief by being drawn elsewhere.
senses.whyCN: 「唤走」正是关键：被引向别处从而得到喘息。

senses.title: An avocation turned profession
senses.definition: a hobby in the process of becoming one's vocation
senses.definitionCN: 正在转变为职业的爱好
senses.example: Her photography avocation grew into a studio.
senses.exampleCN: 她的摄影爱好后来发展成一间影楼。
senses.why: The word sits on the border; people cross it.
senses.whyCN: 这个词立在边界上，而人们会跨越边界。

senses.title: The respectable dilettante sphere
senses.definition: the cultivated amateur sphere, as in an avocation of gentlemen scholars
senses.definitionCN: 绅士学者的风雅业余领域
senses.example: Botany was a fashionable avocation in the eighteenth century.
senses.exampleCN: 18 世纪，植物学是时髦的雅趣。
senses.why: Amateur once meant lover: the avocation of those who could afford to love.
senses.whyCN: amateur 本义是「爱好者」：avocation 属于有闲去爱的人们。

senses.title: Legal sense, a calling away
senses.definition: in older legal language, the removal of a case or person to another jurisdiction
senses.definitionCN: 旧法律用语，指将案件或人员移转他辖
senses.example: An avocation of the suit shifted it to chancery.
senses.exampleCN: 案件移转后归大法官庭审理。
senses.why: The root verb avocare lived in legal Latin for summoning away.
senses.whyCN: 词根动词 avocare 在法律拉丁语中即「传唤他去」。

senses.title: A pleasurable identity
senses.definition: the self one becomes through a beloved sideline
senses.definitionCN: 借由热爱的副业获得的另一种自我身份
senses.example: At the easel he was someone else: the painter of his avocation.
senses.exampleCN: 画架前他成了另一个人：副业里的画家。
senses.why: A calling-away calls up a second self to answer it.
senses.whyCN: 被唤走时，会有第二个自我起身应答。

intro.en: Avocation comes from Latin avocatio, a calling away, from avocare, from ab, away, plus vocare, to call; English took the word in the fifteenth century, at first near its legal sense.
intro.cn: avocation 出自拉丁语 avocatio「唤走」，由 avocare 构成，后者为 ab（离开）+ vocare（呼唤）；英语于 15 世纪借入，起初贴近其法律义。

items.en: The call-root is the reconstructed wek-, to speak or call out.
items.cn: 「呼唤」词根出自重构词干 wek-「说、喊」。

items.en: avocare combined ab, away, with vocare, to call: to summon someone off.
items.cn: avocare 组合 ab「离开」与 vocare「呼唤」：把人召走。

items.en: avocatio meant a diversion, distraction, or legal removal.
items.cn: avocatio 指消遣、分心，或法律上的移转。

items.en: Middle English used avocation for distraction and for calling off a case.
items.cn: 中古英语用 avocation 表分心及案件撤移。

items.en: The hobby sense consolidated, paired against vocation in Victorian prose.
items.cn: 17 至 19 世纪「爱好」义定型，维多利亚散文常将其与 vocation 对举。

items.en: Today the pairing avocation and vocation is the word's classic frame.
items.cn: 如今 avocation 与 vocation 的对举是这个词的经典语境。

note.en: Group one gathers the vocare family and its call-aways; group two gathers the work-and-play scale.
note.cn: 第一组收 vocare 词族及诸「唤走」词；第二组收工作与消遣刻度上的词。

entries.definition: the main calling, one prefix away and opposite in rank.
entries.definitionCN: 主业、天职；仅一个前缀之差，位阶相反。

entries.definition: the act of summoning a memory or feeling; shares vocare, not the hobby sense.
entries.definitionCN: 唤起记忆或情感；共享 vocare 词根，但与爱好无关。

entries.definition: a rare obsolete form of advocacy; one letter from avocation.
entries.definitionCN: advocacy 的罕见废形；与 avocation 仅差一个字母。

entries.definition: the plain everyday word for a pastime.
entries.definitionCN: 消遣的日常普通说法。

entries.definition: an activity that makes time pass pleasantly.
entries.definitionCN: 消磨时光的活动。

entries.definition: a secondary money-earning activity.
entries.definitionCN: 有副收入的第二营生。

entries.definition: something that turns the mind aside for relief.
entries.definitionCN: 让心思转向以获休息之物。

entries.definition: an occupation, main or spare-time, formal register.
entries.definitionCN: 营生或消遣，正式语域。

normalIntro.en: Split it a-vo-ca-tion: a calling away from your vocation.
normalIntro.cn: 拆成 a-vo-ca-tion 记：从主业里被唤走的那一声呼唤。

normal.en: vocare means to call; vocation calls you to work, avocation calls you away.
normal.cn: vocare 意为呼唤：vocation 把你唤去上班，avocation 把你唤走。

normal.en: ab- away plus vocare call: the same ab- as in avert.
normal.cn: ab- 离开 + vocare 呼唤；ab- 与 avert 中相同。

normal.en: Classic pairing: avocation and vocation.
normal.cn: 经典对举：avocation 与 vocation。

normal.en: by avocation a lawyer means he practices law, loves something else.
normal.cn: by avocation 的句式：以某事为业余爱好。

normal.en: Spelling trap: not advocation; there is no d.
normal.cn: 拼写陷阱：中间没有 d，不是 advocation。

abstract.en: Hear the workday phone ring, and the little bell of the workbench answer.
abstract.cn: 听工作日的电话在响，工作台的小铃也答了一声。

abstract.en: An avocation is the room your other self keeps.
abstract.cn: avocation 是你的另一个自我常住的房间。

abstract.en: Picture the briefcase set down beside a wooden flute.
abstract.cn: 想象公文包被放下，旁边是一支木笛。

examples.en: Taxidermy was the naturalist's strange avocation.
examples.cn: 标本剥制是那位博物学家的怪癖爱好。

examples.en: She hoped to turn her avocation into a full-time vocation.
examples.cn: 她希望把业余爱好变成全职事业。

examples.en: Chess, by avocation, sharpened his courtroom thinking.
examples.cn: 作为业余爱好的国际象棋磨利了他法庭上的思维。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「爱我开心」——爱我开心的事就是我的业余爱好

root: 出自拉丁语 avocatio「唤走、消遣」，由 avocare（ab- 离开 + vocare 呼唤）构成，与 vocation 同根而加相反方向的前缀；15 世纪进入英语，先用于法律与「分心」义，17 世纪起「业余爱好」义成为主流。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses pivot on being called away: the hobby, the side job, the old legal summoning, the relief of diversion, and the second self a pastime can create.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项围绕「被唤走」展开：爱好、副业、旧法律上的传唤、消遣的喘息，以及爱好塑造的第二重自我。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a voice calling you off the main road onto a small bright path.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个声音把你从大路唤向小径。

definition_zh: 适应；改编；改写本；（生物）适应
definition_en: the process of adjusting to new conditions, or a version of a work changed for a new medium
core_image: 一件旧衣被改短，穿到了另一个身上
scene: 剧团把一本厚小说搬上舞台，台词删去大半，灯光也换了风格。 The stage adaption cut the long novel into two hours.
sceneCN: 这里 adaption 是「改编」（第 1 个义项：把作品改成另一种表现形式）；句意为这次舞台改编把长篇小说压缩成两个小时。

pos.zh: 名词：适应；改编；改写本

derivatives.zh: 本词的动词基础，义为「适应；改编」
与本词同义的更常见拼写形式，义为「适应；改编」
由 adapt 加 -ive 构成，义为「适应性的」
由 adaptive 加 -ability 构成，义为「适应能力」
由 adapt 加 -er 构成，义为「改编者；适配器」

senses.title: The process of adjusting
senses.definition: the process of changing in order to fit new conditions or a new purpose
senses.definitionCN: 为适应新条件或新用途而作出改变的过程
senses.example: The adaption of the old team to the new software took a month.
senses.exampleCN: 旧团队适应新软件花了一个月。
senses.why: Adapt means to fit, and -ion names the process, so adaption is the act of making something fit.
senses.whyCN: adapt 意为「使适合」，-ion 表示过程，所以 adaption 就是「使某物适合」的行为。

senses.title: A changed version
senses.definition: a product that has been modified to suit a new use or audience
senses.definitionCN: 为适应新用途或新受众而修改过的成品
senses.example: The children's adaption keeps the story but simplifies the language.
senses.exampleCN: 儿童版改写保留了故事，但简化了语言。
senses.why: Once the process is finished, the word can name the finished thing, just as a translation names its result.
senses.whyCN: 过程完成后，这个词可以指完成的成品，就像 translation 也指译出的作品。

senses.title: Biological adaptation
senses.definition: an inherited feature or change that helps an organism survive in its environment
senses.definitionCN: 帮助生物在环境中存活的遗传特征或变化
senses.example: The thick coat is an adaption to the long northern winter.
senses.exampleCN: 厚皮毛是对漫长北方冬季的一种适应。
senses.why: Living things fit themselves to their surroundings over generations, so the general idea becomes a biological term.
senses.whyCN: 生物在世代之间使自己适合环境，于是这个一般概念成了生物学术语。

senses.title: A film or stage version
senses.definition: a play, film or television version of a novel, story or other source work
senses.definitionCN: 把小说、故事或其他原作改成戏剧、电影或电视的版本
senses.example: The film adaption moved the ending to a different city.
senses.exampleCN: 电影改编把结局搬到了另一座城市。
senses.why: A book must be fitted to a new medium, and the result is called by the same word as the fitting process.
senses.whyCN: 一本书必须被改造以适合新媒介，成品与改造过程共用同一个词。

senses.title: Sensory adaptation
senses.definition: the weakening of a sensation after continuous exposure to the same stimulus
senses.definitionCN: 持续接触同一刺激后感觉逐渐减弱的现象
senses.example: Sensory adaption explains why the noise seems quieter after an hour.
senses.exampleCN: 感觉适应解释了为什么一小时后噪声似乎变小了。
senses.why: The senses adjust their sensitivity to a steady input, which is a literal fitting of the body to conditions.
senses.whyCN: 感官会调整对稳定输入的敏感度，这是身体对条件的字面适应。

senses.title: Social or cultural adjustment
senses.definition: the process of adjusting to a new culture, community or way of life
senses.definitionCN: 适应新文化、新社区或新生活方式的过程
senses.example: Her adaption to the new school was helped by a host family.
senses.exampleCN: 寄宿家庭帮助她适应了新学校。
senses.why: People fit themselves to social surroundings, so the word covers the human version of fitting.
senses.whyCN: 人会让自己适合社会环境，所以这个词也涵盖「人适应环境」这一版本。

senses.title: A technical modification
senses.definition: a change made to a machine, system or device so it can serve a new purpose
senses.definitionCN: 为使机器、系统或装置服务新用途而作的改动
senses.example: The adaption of the pump for salt water required new seals.
senses.exampleCN: 把水泵改装用于海水需要新的密封件。
senses.why: Tools are fitted to new jobs by physical change, which is the engineering branch of the same idea.
senses.whyCN: 工具通过物理改动去适合新任务，这是同一理念在工程上的分支。

senses.title: A spelling variant
senses.definition: the less common spelling of adaptation, used chiefly in some technical and older texts
senses.definitionCN: adaptation 的较少见拼写，主要用于部分技术文献与较早文本
senses.example: Some journals use adaption, though adaptation is now the standard form.
senses.exampleCN: 有些期刊使用 adaption，不过 adaptation 现在是标准形式。
senses.why: English often drops or keeps a Latin suffix by fashion, so the shorter form survives as a recognized variant.
senses.whyCN: 英语常按习惯省略或保留拉丁后缀，于是较短的形式作为被承认的变体留存下来。

intro.en: Adaption and adaptation both rest on the Latin verb adaptare, to fit; the shorter form is an English variant.
intro.cn: adaption 与 adaptation 都建立在拉丁语动词 adaptare「使适合」之上；较短的形式是英语变体。

items.en: Aptus meant fit, suited or fastened; it is also the source of apt and aptitude.
items.cn: aptus 意为「合适的、贴合的」，也是 apt 与 aptitude 的来源。

items.en: Ad plus aptare formed adaptare, to fit something to something else.
items.cn: ad 与 aptare 构成 adaptare，意为「使某物适合另一物」。

items.en: The verb adapt entered English through French; the exact first date is uncertain.
items.cn: 动词 adapt 经由法语进入英语，确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: Adaptation was formed with -ation; the shorter adaption appeared as a variant spelling.
items.cn: adaptation 由 -ation 构成；较短的 adaption 作为变体拼写出现。

items.en: With evolutionary theory, adaptation became a central biological term for features that fit an environment.
items.cn: 随着进化论，adaptation 成为生物学的核心术语，指适合环境的特征。

items.en: Adaptation dominates standard usage, while adaption survives in technical and older writing.
items.cn: 现代标准用法以 adaptation 为主，adaption 则留存于技术文献与较早写作中。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the adapt family and its spelling double; the near-meaning group gathers words for change and versions of works.
note.cn: 形近组收 adapt 词族及其拼写双体；近义组收表示改变与作品版本的词。

entries.definition: The standard spelling of the same word, more common in modern English.
entries.definitionCN: 同一词的标准化拼写，在现代英语中更常见。

entries.definition: The verb meaning to adjust or change to fit.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「适应；改编」，是本词的核心动词。

entries.definition: The adjective meaning able to adjust to new conditions.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「适应性的、能调整的」。

entries.definition: The noun for the quality of being able to adapt.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「适应能力」。

entries.definition: A person who adapts a work, or a device that connects different fittings.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「改编者」或「适配器」。

entries.definition: A change made to fit a new situation; often smaller and more mechanical than adaption.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「调整」，常指较小、更机械的改动，范围比 adaption 窄。

entries.definition: A form of something that differs from other forms; it does not imply fitting to a new medium.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「版本」，指与其他形式不同的形态，不必然暗示媒介转换。

entries.definition: A work moved from one language to another; a sibling idea to adaptation across media.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「翻译」，指把作品从一种语言搬到另一种语言，与跨媒介改编同类。

entries.definition: A partial change; broader than adaption and with no goal of fitting.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「修改」，指部分改动，范围更宽且不必然以适合为目的。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real aptus root and the media and biology phrases the word appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子使用真实的 aptus 词根，以及这个词实际出现的媒介与生物搭配。

normal.en: Adaptare is ad plus aptare, to fit one thing to another.
normal.cn: adaptare 是 ad 加 aptare，意为「把一物配到另一物上」。

normal.en: Apt and aptitude share the same fit root, so adapt is about fitting, not random change.
normal.cn: apt 与 aptitude 共享同一个「合适」词根，所以 adapt 讲的是贴合，不是随意改变。

normal.en: Adaptation is the standard spelling; adaption is the shorter variant.
normal.cn: adaptation 是标准拼写；adaption 是较短的变体。

normal.en: A film adaption fits a book to the screen.
normal.cn: film adaption 是把书「配到」银幕上。

normal.en: A biological adaption fits an organism to its habitat.
normal.cn: biological adaption 是让生物适合其栖息地。

abstract.en: Picture an old coat with the sleeves shortened, then handed to a smaller wearer.
abstract.cn: 想象一件旧外套被改短袖子，然后递给个子更小的人穿。

abstract.en: Adaption is not copying and not destroying: it keeps the material and changes the fit.
abstract.cn: 改编既不是复制也不是毁掉：它保留材料，只改变贴合方式。

abstract.en: A story moving from page to stage is the same coat worn in a different room.
abstract.cn: 故事从书页搬到舞台，就像同一件外套穿进另一间屋子。

examples.en: The radio adaption of the novel kept the narrator but cut two characters.
examples.cn: 这部小说的广播改编保留了叙述者，却删掉了两个人物。

examples.en: Her adaption to city life was slow but complete.
examples.cn: 她对城市生活的适应虽慢却彻底。

examples.en: The plant's adaption to dry soil is visible in its narrow leaves.
examples.cn: 这种植物对干燥土壤的适应体现在狭窄的叶片上。

sensesIntro.en: The eight senses all describe fitting one thing to another: a process, a finished version, a species to its habitat, a book to a screen, senses to a stimulus, a person to a culture, a machine to a job, and a spelling to fashion.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都在描述「把一物配到另一物上」：过程、成品、物种与栖息地、书与银幕、感官与刺激、人与文化、机器与任务，以及拼写与习惯。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a coat is shortened at the sleeves and given to a smaller wearer.
core.cn: 核心意象：外套袖子被改短，交给个子更小的穿者。

branches.en: THE PROCESS: people, cultures and machines adjust to new conditions.
branches.cn: 过程线：人、文化与机器适应新条件。

branches.en: THE VERSION: a finished work or product made to fit a new medium.
branches.cn: 版本线：为适合新媒介而完成的成品。

branches.en: THE BODY: biology and the senses fit organisms to their surroundings.
branches.cn: 身体线：生物学与感官让生物适合环境。

branches.en: THE SPELLING: the shorter form survives beside the standard one.
branches.cn: 拼写线：较短形式与标准形式并存。

branches.en: THE NAME: process and product share one word, as in translation.
branches.cn: 命名线：过程与成品共用一个词，正如 translation。

definition_en: the process or moment in which a young animal breaks out of its egg, or a set of fine parallel lines used for shading
core_image: 蛋壳顶端出现第一条细缝，一小块壳被顶开，湿漉漉的头先探出来，壳还挂在背上
scene: 巢里的卵已经放了十九天，今天早晨第一枚壳上出现了一道裂缝。 Hatching takes most of a day, and the chick stays wet and weak for hours after it.
sceneCN: 这里 hatching 指「出壳、破壳的过程」（第 1 个义项：幼体用喙或牙顶破卵壳而出的过程）；句意为出壳要花大半天，雏鸟出壳后数小时仍湿而虚弱。
