senses.title: Breaking out of the egg
senses.definition: the moment or process in which a young animal breaks the shell and leaves the egg
senses.definitionCN: 幼体破开卵壳并离开卵的那一刻或过程
senses.example: Hatching takes most of a day for this species.
senses.exampleCN: 这个物种出壳要花大半天。
senses.why: the -ing form names the event as an unfolding process, which suits a break that is gradual rather than instantaneous.
senses.whyCN: -ing 形式把事件看作逐步展开的过程，适合这种并非瞬间完成的破壳。

senses.title: The whole hatching period of a clutch
senses.definition: the stretch of time over which all eggs in a nest break
senses.definitionCN: 一巢中所有卵破壳所跨的那段时间
senses.example: Hatching stretched over three days because laying began early.
senses.exampleCN: 由于产卵开始得早，出壳持续了三天。
senses.why: eggs laid at different times break at different times, so the event extends into a period.
senses.whyCN: 不同时间产下的卵在不同时间破壳，因此事件延伸成一段时期。

senses.title: The success rate of a hatching attempt
senses.definition: the proportion of eggs that produce live young, as recorded in field studies
senses.definitionCN: 在野外研究中记录的、成功孵出活幼体的卵所占比例
senses.example: Hatching fell to half after the cold snap.
senses.exampleCN: 寒潮之后孵化率掉到一半。
senses.why: field workers count eggs in and chicks out, so the event becomes a measurable quantity.
senses.whyCN: 野外工作者数进出的卵与雏，事件于是成为可测量的量。

senses.title: Staggered hatching in one nest
senses.definition: the condition in which eggs in one clutch break at intervals rather than together
senses.definitionCN: 同一窝卵按间隔而非同时破壳的情形
senses.example: Staggered hatching gives the oldest chick an advantage.
senses.exampleCN: 不同步出壳让最年长的雏占优势。
senses.why: the word needs only a qualifier to describe timing, since the event itself is unchanged.
senses.whyCN: 只需加一个限定语即可描述时间安排，因为事件本身没有变化。

senses.title: The first food and first steps after hatching
senses.titleCN: 出壳后的最初进食与行动
senses.definition: the early post-hatching stage in which a young animal learns to feed and move
senses.definitionCN: 幼体学习取食与行动的最初阶段
senses.example: Hatching is followed by a day of drying out before any feeding.
senses.exampleCN: 出壳之后要先晾干一天才开始进食。
senses.why: the word is used as a fixed point that later stages are measured from.
senses.whyCN: 这个词被当作一个固定时间点，后续阶段都从它起算。

senses.title: Art: parallel lines used for shading
senses.titleCN: 美术：用平行细线作阴影
senses.definition: in drawing and engraving, a set of closely spaced parallel lines that create tone
senses.definitionCN: 绘画与版画中一组密集平行线，用来制造明暗层次
senses.example: Fine hatching gives the cheek its roundness.
senses.exampleCN: 细密的晕线让面颊显出圆润。
senses.why: the older artistic sense comes from hatching as cutting lines into a surface, and it survives unchanged in studio vocabulary.
senses.whyCN: 较早的美术义来自在表面上刻划线条的 hatching，这一义在画室术语中完整保留。

senses.title: Crossed lines for deeper shadow
senses.definition: two or more sets of hatching laid over each other to darken an area
senses.definitionCN: 两组或更多排线叠在一起使某区域更暗
senses.example: Cross hatching turned the corner of the wall almost black.
senses.exampleCN: 交叉排线把墙角压得几乎全黑。
senses.why: the compound merely states that the lines cross, so the base meaning is unchanged.
senses.whyCN: 复合词只说线是交叉的，词基意义并无改变。

senses.title: Figurative: a secret being prepared
senses.titleCN: 比喻：秘密正在被酝酿出来
senses.definition: figurative, the developing stage of a plot or scheme before it is revealed
senses.definitionCN: 比喻用法，指阴谋或计划在公开之前的发展阶段
senses.example: They were hatching a plan all winter in the back room.
senses.exampleCN: 他们整个冬天都在后屋里悄悄策划一个方案。
senses.why: the metaphor keeps the image of something growing out of sight until it suddenly appears.
senses.whyCN: 比喻保留了「某物在看不见处长成，然后突然出现」的意象。

intro.en: Hatching is the -ing form of hatch, a Germanic verb with a disputed deeper origin and a separate artistic sense.
intro.cn: hatching 是 hatch 的 -ing 形式；hatch 是日耳曼动词，其更深来源有争议，另有一条独立的美术义。

items.en: Middle English hacche meant the act of brooding and of breaking the shell; the form is shared with Middle Dutch and Middle Low German.
items.cn: 中古英语 hacche 指伏窝与破壳的行为，其形式与中古荷兰语、中古低地德语共有。

items.en: The Germanic verb carried the idea of producing young from an egg, and also of cutting lines, which produced the artistic sense.
items.cn: 这个日耳曼动词带「由卵生幼」的意思，也带「刻划线条」的意思，后者产生了美术义。

items.en: Source uncertain (root): the pre-Germanic origin of hatch is unresolved; the common Indo-European form quoted for it is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（词根）：hatch 在日耳曼语之前的来源无定论；常引的印欧形式属重构。

items.en: From the fifteenth century hatching named short parallel strokes in drawing, probably from the idea of cutting or striking lines.
items.cn: 自 15 世纪起，hatching 指绘画中的短平行笔触，可能源自「刻、划线条」的想法。

items.en: The -ing form became the standard name for the event, so field reports speak of hatching success and hatching date.
items.cn: -ing 形式成为事件的标准名称，因此野外报告说 hatching success 与 hatching date。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date): the earliest record of hatching in its technical sense is not firmly dated, and the link between the two senses is inferred rather than documented.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代）：hatching 技术义的最早书证年代不确定，两个义项之间的联系属推断，未见直接文献。

note.en: Group one separates the hatch family; group two separates the biological hatching from the stages around it.
note.cn: 第一组区分 hatch 词族；第二组区分生物学意义上的出壳与其前后阶段。

entries.definition: The bare verb is to break out or to plan secretly; as a noun it is a hatchway or opening, not the process.
entries.definitionCN: 原形动词指破壳或秘密策划；作名词指舱口、开口，而不是这一过程。

entries.definition: A hatchling is the animal just out of the egg; hatching is the event, hatchling is its result.
entries.definitionCN: hatchling 是刚出壳的动物；hatching 是事件，hatchling 是其结果。

entries.definition: A hatchery is where eggs are hatched commercially; the -ery suffix marks a place of activity.
entries.definitionCN: hatchery 是商业孵卵的场所；-ery 后缀标记活动场所。

entries.definition: Hatchback names a car body style by its rear hatch; it has nothing to do with eggs.
entries.definitionCN: hatchback 以车尾舱门命名一种车身式样，与卵无关。

entries.definition: Incubation is the warming period that ends in hatching, so the two are consecutive stages.
entries.definitionCN: incubation 是以出壳收尾的保温期，两者是连续的两个阶段。

entries.definition: Emergence is any coming out, including insects from pupae; hatching is specific to eggs.
entries.definitionCN: emergence 泛指任何出现，包括昆虫自蛹中出来；hatching 专指自卵而出。

entries.definition: Eclosion is the entomologist's word for emerging from an egg or pupa, narrower than hatching.
entries.definitionCN: eclosion 是昆虫学中自卵或蛹出来的术语，比 hatching 更窄。

entries.definition: Stippling is shading made of dots; hatching is shading made of lines, a common confusion in drawing.
entries.definitionCN: stippling 用点作阴影；hatching 用线作阴影，素描中常混。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphology, real field terms and real studio vocabulary.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实形态、真实现场术语与真实画室词汇。

normal.en: hatch + -ing: the verb of breaking out turned into the name of the event.
normal.cn: hatch + -ing：破壳动词转为事件名称。

normal.en: The family runs hatch, hatching, hatchling, hatchery, hatched.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 hatch、hatching、hatchling、hatchery、hatched。

normal.en: Field phrases: hatching success, hatching date, hatching asynchrony.
normal.cn: 现场搭配：孵化成功率、出壳日期、不同步出壳。

normal.en: In drawing, cross hatching darkens an area with two sets of lines.
normal.cn: 在素描中，交叉排线用两组线把区域压暗。

normal.en: The idiom hatch a plan reuses the egg image for secrets.
normal.cn: 习语 hatch a plan 把卵的意象用于秘密。

abstract.en: Picture a crack that spreads slowly, then suddenly gives way.
abstract.cn: 想象一道裂缝慢慢延伸，然后突然让开。

abstract.en: Picture two kinds of shade, one drawn with dots, one with strokes.
abstract.cn: 想象两种阴影，一种用点画，一种用笔画。

abstract.en: Picture a plan growing in the dark until the day it is spoken aloud.
abstract.cn: 想象一个计划在暗处长成，直到被说出口的那一天。

examples.en: Hatching began at dawn and was over by noon.
examples.cn: 出壳在黎明开始，中午前结束。

examples.en: The engraver used dense hatching for the shadowed half of the face.
examples.cn: 版画师用密集晕线处理脸部的暗面。

examples.en: Cold nights can delay hatching by nearly a week.
examples.cn: 寒夜可让出壳推迟将近一周。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「hatch（破壳）+ ing」——壳破小兽出 → 出壳、孵化；美术义为一条条排出的线

root: 中古英语 hacche「孵、破壳」，与中古荷兰语、中古低地德语同形，属日耳曼词；美术义「刻划线条」为另一条引申线；日耳曼语之前的词根来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one break: a shell splits and something wet emerges, and the word then names the period, the success rate, the timing pattern, the stage after it, two kinds of drawn line, and finally a plan that emerges the same way.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿一次破裂展开：壳裂开，一个湿漉漉的东西出来；词语随后指这段时期、成功率、时间格局、其后阶段、两种描画线条，最后指以同样方式出现的计划。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the first crack at the top of an egg, and a wet head pushing through it.
core.cn: 核心意象：卵顶的第一道裂缝，一颗湿漉漉的头从中顶出。

branches.en: EMERGENCE: the literal break and the figurative plan share one shape.
branches.cn: 出现：字面的破壳与比喻的计划共享同一形状。

branches.en: TIMING: eggs break at intervals, so the event expands into a schedule.
branches.cn: 时序：卵按间隔破壳，事件于是扩展成一张时间表。

branches.en: COUNTED RESULT: what comes out can be counted against what went in.
branches.cn: 可数的结果：出来的可以与进去的对照计数。

branches.en: MARKER POINT: later stages are dated from the break.
branches.cn: 标记点：后续阶段从破壳起算。

branches.en: CUT LINES: the studio sense shades with strokes, crossed or single.
branches.cn: 刻线：画室义用单层或交叉的笔触作阴影。

intro.en: Hatching is a native verb plus the English -ing ending; its artistic sense grew inside English, not from Latin.
intro.cn: hatching 是本族动词加英语 -ing 词尾；美术义是在英语内部长成的，并非来自拉丁语。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin element in hatch; the Latin entries below are the learned words English borrowed separately for hatching and for emerging.
latinIntro.cn: hatch 不含拉丁成分；下列拉丁条目是英语为「孵化」与「出现」另行借入的学术词。

items.meaning: to break out of an egg
items.example: The first egg hatched at dawn.
The hatchling could not stand yet.
The hatchery releases fry into the river.
items.exampleCN: 孵化场把鱼苗放流到河里。

items.example: The hatched chicks were moved to a brooder.
items.exampleCN: 已出壳的雏被移进育雏箱。

items.meaning: the rate of eggs that produce young
items.example: Hatching success dropped after the flood.
items.exampleCN: 洪水之后孵化成功率下降。

items.example: They hatched a plan over the winter.
items.exampleCN: 他们在冬天里策划了一套方案。

latinEntries.meaning: to shut out; of a chick, to hatch out

latinEntries.structure: ovum, ovi (n., second declension, plural ova)

definition_zh: 本能的；直觉的；不假思索的；与生俱来的
definition_en: based on or produced by instinct rather than by reasoning, learning or deliberate choice
core_image: 手离滚烫的锅还有一寸时已经缩回，动作比意识更早一步
scene: 孩子第一次看见盘起来的绳子就立刻缩手后退，还没来得及判断那到底是什么。 The child withdrew from the coiled rope before any reasoned check, an instinctive response to a shape that resembles a threat.
sceneCN: 这里 instinctive 指「由本能驱动、不经理性判断的反应」（第 1 个义项：源自本能而非推理的反应）；句意为孩子还没来得及辨认就缩手后退，那是对形似威胁之物的一种本能反应。可辨识物件：盘起的绳子、缩回的手、孩子的侧脸。

pos.zh: 本能的；出于本能的
直觉的；不假思索的
与生俱来的；天生的

forms.label: 同义形容词（心理学常用）

senses.title: Produced by instinct, not reasoning
senses.titleCN: 由本能而非推理产生的
senses.definition: coming from an inborn drive rather than from conscious thought
senses.definitionCN: 源自天生的驱力，而非有意识的思考
senses.example: Her instinctive grip on the rail saved her from the fall.
senses.exampleCN: 她本能地抓住栏杆，才没有摔下去。
senses.why: The suffix -ive turns the noun into a description of what a reaction comes from, so instinctive marks the source of the act: instinct, not judgement.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -ive 把名词转为描述反应来源的形容词，因此 instinctive 标出动作的来源：是本能，不是判断。

senses.title: Done without deliberation
senses.definition: happening so quickly that no deliberate weighing of options takes place
senses.definitionCN: 发生得太快，根本没有对选项作有意的权衡
senses.example: He gave an instinctive nod before he had heard the whole offer.
senses.exampleCN: 他还没听完整个提议就本能地点了头。
senses.why: What comes from instinct arrives before deliberation can finish; the adjective therefore also describes the speed of the act.
senses.whyCN: 出于本能的东西在斟酌完成前就到了，因此这个形容词也描述动作的速度。

senses.title: Innate rather than acquired
senses.definition: present from birth rather than built up by training or experience
senses.definitionCN: 自出生起就有，而非经训练或经验积累形成
senses.example: The paper asks whether rhythm is instinctive or learned.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇论文追问节奏感是天生的还是学来的。
senses.why: Instinct names what an animal has without learning, so the adjective naturally marks the boundary between nature and training.
senses.whyCN: instinct 指动物不经学习就有的东西，因此这个形容词自然用来划出天性与训练的界线。

senses.title: Unlearned behaviour in ethology
senses.titleCN: 行为学意义上的非学习行为
senses.definition: in ethology, describing a fixed response elicited by a sign stimulus without prior experience
senses.definitionCN: 在行为学中，描述由信号刺激引发、无需先前经验的固定反应
senses.example: The team recorded an instinctive pecking sequence in chicks raised alone.
senses.exampleCN: 研究组记录了单独饲养的雏鸟身上那套本能的啄食序列。
senses.why: Ethologists adopted the adjective for behaviour that isolation cannot erase, giving the everyday word a controlled technical use.
senses.whyCN: 行为学家用这个形容词指隔离也抹不掉的行为，使日常词获得受控的术语用法。

senses.title: Automatic in style
senses.definition: describing a movement or judgement so practised that it feels automatic
senses.definitionCN: 形容动作或判断熟练到近乎自动
senses.example: Years of practice had made his footwork instinctive.
senses.exampleCN: 多年练习使他的步法近乎自动。
senses.why: Training can make a learned skill feel unlearned; the adjective then borrows the sense of 'effortless' from its core meaning.
senses.whyCN: 训练能让学来的技艺感觉像没学过；这个形容词于是从核心义借来「不费力」的意思。

senses.title: Deeply rooted in character
senses.definition: describing a tendency that seems part of a person's basic nature
senses.definitionCN: 形容某种倾向仿佛是某人基本天性的一部分
senses.example: His instinctive distrust of slogans never left him.
senses.exampleCN: 他对口号那种本能的不信任从未离开过他。
senses.why: If instinct can be treated as a part of the self, the adjective can describe traits that feel inseparable from who someone is.
senses.whyCN: 既然本能可被当作自我的一部分，这个形容词就能描述那些仿佛与某人不可分割的特质。

senses.title: Immediate and unreasoned in judgement
senses.titleCN: 判断上即时且未经理性的
senses.definition: of a judgement, reached at once and without explicit evidence
senses.definitionCN: 形容判断当即作出、没有明示证据
senses.example: Reviewers often reach an instinctive verdict in the first ten seconds.
senses.exampleCN: 评审者常在最初十秒就作出本能的判断。
senses.why: The word can describe verdicts as well as movements: what is instant and unreasoned looks the same whether it is a hand or an opinion.
senses.whyCN: 这个词既能形容动作也能形容判断：无论缩手还是形成意见，即时而不经理性的样子是一样的。

senses.title: Abstract: belonging to the nature of a thing
senses.titleCN: 抽象义：属于事物本性的
senses.definition: used of a quality that appears to belong to the very nature of something
senses.definitionCN: 用于形容某种仿佛属于事物本性的特质
senses.example: The novelist treats loyalty as instinctive in dogs and negotiable in people.
senses.exampleCN: 这位小说家把忠诚写成狗的本性，而在人身上则可有可无。
senses.why: At its widest, the adjective no longer needs a creature: any quality said to be built into a thing's nature can be called instinctive.
senses.whyCN: 在最宽泛的用法里，这个形容词不再需要生命体：任何被称为「天生嵌在事物本性里」的特质都可叫 instinctive。

intro.en: Instinctive is an English adjective formed on the Latin participle stem instinct- plus the suffix -ive. It appears in the 1640s, and its adverb instinctively follows within a few decades.
intro.cn: instinctive 是英语形容词，由拉丁分词词干 instinct- 加后缀 -ive 构成，17 世纪 40 年代出现，其副词 instinctively 在数十年内随之出现。

items.en: The stem comes from instinctus, the past participle of instinguere 'to incite, goad', so the adjective inherits the image of something driven in.
items.cn: 该词干来自 instinctus，即 instinguere「煽动、驱赶」的过去分词，因此这个形容词继承了「被推入」的意象。

items.en: Latin -ivus formed adjectives of tendency or function; English -ive does the same, as in active, decisive and instinctive.
items.cn: 拉丁 -ivus 构成表示倾向或功能的形容词；英语 -ive 作用相同，如 active、decisive、instinctive。

items.en: The adjective is recorded from the 1640s, built directly on the noun rather than borrowed whole from a Latin adjective.
items.cn: 该形容词自 17 世纪 40 年代有记录，直接由名词构成，而非整体借自某个拉丁形容词。

items.en: Instinctively is recorded from the 1610s in the sources, and instinctiveness follows; the family kept growing by ordinary English suffixation.
items.cn: 据所查资料，instinctively 自 17 世纪 10 年代有记录，instinctiveness 随之出现；这个词族靠普通英语后缀不断扩展。

items.en: Nineteenth- and twentieth-century biology gave the adjective a technical role in descriptions of unlearned behaviour.
items.cn: 19 至 20 世纪的生物学赋予这个形容词描述非学习行为的技术角色。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date): dictionaries differ on whether the earliest citation for instinctively belongs to the 1610s or later, and the pre-Latin origin of stinguere remains a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代）：各词典对 instinctively 最早书证属于 17 世纪 10 年代还是更晚并不一致；stinguere 在拉丁语之前的来源仍属重构。

note.en: Group one distinguishes adjectives that look related but are built on other stems; group two holds near synonyms that differ in whether they stress origin, speed or feeling.
note.cn: 第一组区分看似相关、其实由别的词干构成的形容词；第二组是近义词，区别在于强调来源、速度还是感受。

entries.definition: A later variant built with -ual instead of -ive; psychology prefers it, but the meaning is essentially the same.
entries.definitionCN: 后出的变体，用 -ual 而非 -ive 构成；心理学更偏爱它，但意思基本相同。

entries.definition: From Latin intueri 'to look at'; it describes knowing by direct perception, with no inborn drive implied.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 intueri「观看」；描述靠直接感知而知晓，不含天生驱力之意。

entries.definition: From distinguere 'to separate', not stinguere 'to prick': it means marking something off as different.
entries.definitionCN: 来自 distinguere「区分」，而非 stinguere「刺」：意为把某物标出、使之有别。

entries.definition: Built on the 'quench' verb behind extinguish; it means tending to put out or wipe out, not inborn.
entries.definitionCN: 由构成 extinguish 的「熄灭」动词构成；意为倾向于熄灭或消灭，与天生无关。

entries.definition: Working by itself without conscious control; it stresses mechanism, while instinctive stresses biological origin.
entries.definitionCN: 无需意识控制自行运作；强调机制，instinctive 强调生物来源。

entries.definition: Happening without the will's consent, as a sneeze; it says nothing about whether the source is inborn.
entries.definitionCN: 未经意志同意就发生，如打喷嚏；不涉及来源是否天生。

entries.definition: Present from birth, from Latin innatus; it describes the possession, not the reaction that flows from it.
entries.definitionCN: 自出生就有，来自拉丁 innatus；描述所拥有的特质，而非由之产生的反应。

entries.definition: Informal for a predictably automatic reaction; it carries criticism that instinctive does not.
entries.definitionCN: 对可预料自动反应的口语说法；带有 instinctive 所没有的贬义。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: instinct + -ive: the adjective simply says 'coming from instinct'.
normal.cn: instinct + -ive：这个形容词只是说「来自本能」。

normal.en: The family runs instinct, instinctive, instinctively, instinctual, instinctiveness.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 instinct、instinctive、instinctively、instinctual、instinctiveness。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: instinctive reaction, instinctive fear, instinctive avoidance.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：本能反应、本能的恐惧、本能的回避。

normal.en: Intuitive looks similar but comes from intueri 'to look', not from stinguere.
normal.cn: intuitive 看似相近，其实来自 intueri「观看」，并非 stinguere。

normal.en: The adverb instinctively usually sits next to the verb: instinctively ducked, instinctively knew.
normal.cn: 副词 instinctively 通常紧挨动词：本能地低头、本能地知道。

abstract.en: Picture a hand that retreats a heartbeat before the brain files its report.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手在头脑递交报告前的一瞬就已收回。

abstract.en: Picture a door that locks itself the instant it senses heat.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇门一感到热度就自己上锁。

abstract.en: Picture a musician whose fingers find the chord while the mind is still reading the score.
abstract.cn: 想象乐手的手指在头脑还在读谱时就已找到和弦。

examples.en: Pulling her hand from the flame was instinctive.
examples.cn: 把手从火焰上抽回是本能的。

examples.en: He has an instinctive sense of where the story should end.
examples.cn: 他对故事该在哪里结束有一种本能的判断。

examples.en: The chicks showed an instinctive response to the shadow overhead.
examples.cn: 雏鸟对头顶的阴影表现出本能反应。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「instinct（本能）+ ive（……的）」——像被本能推着走一样的 → 本能的、不假思索的

root: instinct（拉丁 instinctus「推动」）+ -ive（拉丁 -ivus，表倾向）；核心为「由内生推动而来」，与 intuitive（intueri 观看）不同源。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses fan out from one claim: the act did not come from reasoning. They then vary the setting, from reflexes and ethology to trained skill, character and abstract nature.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从同一个判断展开：这个动作不来自推理。随后变换场景，从反射与行为学，到训练出的技艺、性格与抽象本性。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a movement that begins before the mind has finished its check.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个在头脑完成核对之前就已开始的行动。

branches.en: SOURCE AND SPEED: the act is traced to instinct, and that origin is what makes it instant.
branches.cn: 来源与速度：动作被追溯到本能，而正是这个来源使它即时。

branches.en: NATURE VERSUS TRAINING: the everyday claim becomes a controlled ethological category.
branches.cn: 天性与训练：日常判断变成受控的行为学范畴。

branches.en: TRAINED TO FEEL UNTRAINED: practice can make a learned movement borrow the look of instinct.
branches.cn: 练到像没练：练习能让学来的动作借来本能的外表。

branches.en: CHARACTER AND VERDICT: the same adjective covers lasting traits and snap judgements.
branches.cn: 性格与判断：同一个形容词既覆盖持久特质，也覆盖瞬间判断。

branches.en: WIDEST SCOPE: any quality felt to belong to a thing's nature.
branches.cn: 最宽的范围：任何被感受为属于事物本性的特质。

intro.en: Instinctive is a transparent derivative: a Latin noun stem plus a Latin adjective suffix, both of which recur across English.
intro.cn: instinctive 是一个透明的派生词：拉丁名词词干加拉丁形容词后缀，两者在英语中反复出现。

latinIntro.en: The stem instinct- goes back to Latin instinctus; -ive goes back to -ivus, the suffix of tendency seen in active and decisive.
latinIntro.cn: 词干 instinct- 可追溯到拉丁 instinctus；-ive 可追溯到 -ivus，即见于 active 与 decisive 的倾向后缀。

items.example: The stem names the source of the reaction.
items.exampleCN: 这个词干点出反应的来源。

items.example: Active, decisive and instinctive share this suffix.
items.exampleCN: active、decisive 与 instinctive 共用这个后缀。

items.example: Judges rated the instinctiveness of each reply.
items.exampleCN: 评审者给每个回答的本能性打了分。
本能的恐惧先于语言出现。

items.example: The study separates learned from non-instinctive responses.
items.exampleCN: 该研究把习得反应与非本能反应分开。

items.example: Critics called the performance technically perfect but uninstinctive.
items.exampleCN: 评论者说这场表演技术上完美，却缺乏本能。

definition_zh: 定价；定价工作；价格体系
definition_en: the activity or system of setting prices for goods and services
core_image: 一张价目表被反复改写，铅笔字迹一层盖着一层，旁边的成本单也在变
scene: 商店后仓里，经理在价目表上来回改动，成本单摊在手边，铅笔痕迹叠了好几层。 Transparent pricing reduced complaints at the counter.
sceneCN: 这里 pricing 指「为商品设定价格的做法与体系」（第 1 个义项：定价这一活动本身）；句意为透明的定价减少了柜台前的投诉。图中可辨识物件：反复改写的价目表、成本单、铅笔、后仓货架。

pos.zh: 定价；定价工作（不可数）；也可作定语，如定价策略、定价模式

senses.title: The work of setting prices
senses.definition: the ongoing activity of deciding what to charge for goods or services
senses.definitionCN: 决定商品或服务收多少钱的持续活动
senses.example: Pricing takes more time than the sales staff expect.
senses.exampleCN: 定价所花的时间比销售人员预想的多。
senses.why: the -ing form names the activity itself, not any single price that results from it.
senses.whyCN: -ing 形式指活动本身，而非由此产生的某一个价格。

senses.title: A firm's price system
senses.definition: the schedule of charges a seller applies across its products
senses.definitionCN: 卖方在其全部商品上采用的价格表
senses.example: Its pricing is simple: one rate for every size.
senses.exampleCN: 它的价格体系很简单：所有规格一个价。
senses.why: pricing can stand for the whole schedule because what is set is a system, not one number.
senses.whyCN: pricing 可以指整张价格表，因为被设定的是体系，而非单一数字。

senses.title: A pricing decision
senses.definition: a specific choice about what to charge, often made at a meeting
senses.definitionCN: 关于收多少钱的具体选择，常在会议上作出
senses.example: The pricing decision was postponed until the cost report arrived.
senses.exampleCN: 定价决策被推迟到成本报告送达之后。
senses.why: business writing uses the gerund attributively for discrete decisions within the activity.
senses.whyCN: 商业写作把这个动名词作定语，指该活动中的一项项具体决策。

senses.title: A method of arriving at a price
senses.definition: the procedure used to calculate a price, such as cost-plus or value-based
senses.definitionCN: 计算价格所用的程序，如成本加成或价值导向
senses.example: Cost-based pricing ignores what buyers are willing to pay.
senses.exampleCN: 成本导向定价忽略买主愿意付多少。
senses.why: the word shifts from the act to the method once analysts compare approaches.
senses.whyCN: 当分析者比较不同做法时，这个词就从动作转向方法。

senses.title: The level at which prices sit
senses.definition: the general height of charges relative to cost or to rivals
senses.definitionCN: 收费相对于成本或对手的总体高度
senses.example: Premium pricing kept the brand's margins high for years.
senses.exampleCN: 溢价定价让这个品牌的利润率多年保持高位。
senses.why: the gerund can name a level as well as an act when the question is how high prices are.
senses.whyCN: 当问题落在价格有多高时，这个动名词也可以指水平，而不只是动作。

senses.title: Dynamic and algorithmic pricing
senses.definition: setting prices by rules or software that change with demand and stock
senses.definitionCN: 由随需求与库存变动的规则或软件来设定价格
senses.example: Airline pricing changes every few minutes as seats sell.
senses.exampleCN: 随着座位售出，航空定价每隔几分钟就变一次。
senses.why: software made price changes continuous, so the activity became a running process rather than an annual decision.
senses.whyCN: 软件使改价连续进行，因此这项活动成了持续过程，而非年度决策。

senses.title: Transfer pricing inside a group
senses.definition: the setting of internal charges between units of the same company
senses.definitionCN: 同一公司各单位之间设定内部收费
senses.example: Transfer pricing rules decide how much profit each country may tax.
senses.exampleCN: 转移定价规则决定每个国家可以征多少利润税。
senses.why: internal prices do not face a market, so the term became a technical branch with its own rules.
senses.whyCN: 内部价格不面对市场，因此这个词成了一个有独立规则的技术分支。

senses.title: Valuing anything scarce
senses.titleCN: 对任何稀缺物的估值（抽象义）
senses.definition: the act of putting a value on time, risk or access rather than on goods
senses.definitionCN: 为时间、风险或准入而非商品标出价值的行为
senses.example: The clinic's pricing of appointments reflects how long each slot is held.
senses.exampleCN: 这家诊所对预约的定价反映了每个时段被占用多久。
senses.why: once anything can be allocated, the word can price it, even without a shelf.
senses.whyCN: 一旦任何东西可以被分配，即使没有货架，这个词也能为其定价。

intro.en: Pricing is English price plus the gerund suffix -ing. Price came through Old French pris from Latin pretium 'price, value, reward'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: pricing 是英语 price 加动名词后缀 -ing 构成。price 经古法语 pris 上溯拉丁 pretium「价格、价值、报酬」。年代均为约数。

items.en: Pretium meant 'price, value, reward'. It is also the source of precious and of the verb appraise, both through the idea of worth.
items.cn: pretium 意为「价格、价值、报酬」。它也是 precious 与动词 appraise 的来源，二者都经「价值」这一概念。

items.en: Old French pris carried the Latin noun into the sense of a stated charge for goods.
items.cn: 古法语 pris 把拉丁名词带入「对商品标出的价钱」这一意义。

items.en: English borrowed price in the thirteenth century, first for the amount asked in a sale and soon for value in general.
items.cn: 英语在 13 世纪借入 price，先指买卖中索要的金额，很快也指一般价值。

items.en: The native suffix -ing formed nouns of action, as in selling and building; pricing is the regular action noun of the verb price.
items.cn: 本族后缀 -ing 构成动作名词，如 selling、building；pricing 是动词 price 的规则动作名词。

items.en: Pricing became a named business function in the twentieth century, when firms separated it from accounting and sales.
items.cn: 20 世纪，企业把定价从会计与销售中分出，pricing 才成为一项有名称的职能。

items.en: The exact first use of pricing as a business term is not recorded; the word form itself is regular and fully documented.
items.cn: pricing 作为商业术语的最早用例没有确切记录；词形本身是规则构成，且有完整书证。

note.en: Group one holds forms from the price family plus two words that look similar but descend differently; group two holds near terms for the work of fixing a charge.
note.cn: 第一组是 price 词族中的词形，外加两个形似但来源不同的词；第二组是表示「确定收费」的近义说法。

entries.definition: The charge itself or the act of setting it; pricing is the ongoing activity or system built on it.
entries.definitionCN: 指收费本身或标价动作；pricing 是建立其上的持续活动或体系。

entries.definition: The participle, used for goods that have already been given a price, as in a priced catalogue.
entries.definitionCN: 过去分词，用于已经标好价的商品，如标价目录。

entries.definition: In the sense of value, prize is a variant of price; in the sense of an award, it comes from French prendre 'to take', a different root.
entries.definitionCN: 在「价值」义上，prize 是 price 的变体；在「奖赏」义上，它来自法语 prendre「拿取」，词根不同。

entries.definition: From ad- plus pretiare 'to value', so it means to assess worth; it is a relative, not a misspelling of apprise.
entries.definitionCN: 来自 ad- 加 pretiare「估价」，意为评估价值；它是同源词，并非 apprise 的错误拼写。

entries.definition: The work of calculating what a product costs to make; pricing starts from cost but also considers demand.
entries.definitionCN: 计算产品制造成本的工作；定价从成本出发，但也考虑需求。

entries.definition: An estimate of the worth of an asset; pricing a product is a narrower commercial case.
entries.definitionCN: 对资产价值的估算；给产品定价是更窄的商业情形。

entries.definition: A price stated for a specific job or order; it is one output of pricing, not the system.
entries.definitionCN: 针对某项工作或订单报出的价格；它是定价的一项产出，而非体系。

entries.definition: Fixing tariffs, often by a regulator for utilities; it is pricing under external control.
entries.definitionCN: 确定费率，常由监管者为公用事业设定；它是受外部控制的定价。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: price + -ing: the activity of putting a charge on goods.
normal.cn: price + -ing：给商品标出价钱的活动。

normal.en: The family runs price, priced, pricey, priceless, overprice, underprice.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 price、priced、pricey、priceless、overprice、underprice。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the business sense: pricing strategy, pricing policy, pricing model.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出商业义：定价策略、定价政策、定价模型。

normal.en: Three common methods are cost-based, value-based and competitor-based.
normal.cn: 三种常见方法是成本导向、价值导向与对手导向。

normal.en: Software made dynamic pricing possible, so prices now move by the minute.
normal.cn: 软件使动态定价成为可能，价格如今按分钟变动。

abstract.en: Picture a price list rewritten until the pencil marks pile up.
abstract.cn: 想象一张价目表被改了又改，铅笔痕迹叠成一层。

abstract.en: Picture a tag that is turned over and over in a shopper's hand.
abstract.cn: 想象一张价签在顾客手里被翻来覆去。

abstract.en: Picture a clock and a price tag wired to the same dial.
abstract.cn: 想象一只钟和一张价签接在同一个表盘上。

examples.en: Pricing is now handled by a team that meets every Monday.
examples.cn: 定价如今由一个每周一开会的团队负责。

examples.en: The company changed its pricing after losing a third of its customers.
examples.cn: 公司在流失三分之一顾客后改变了定价。

examples.en: Transfer pricing rules decide where a multinational's profit is taxed.
examples.cn: 转移定价规则决定跨国企业的利润在哪里纳税。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「price（价格）+ ing（正在做）」——正在给商品定价格 → 定价

root: price 经古法语 pris 上溯拉丁 pretium「价格、价值、报酬」；pricing 为 price 加本族动名词后缀 -ing，指定价活动或价格体系。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one act of numbering: a seller decides what to charge, and that decision is then seen as an activity, a system, a discrete decision, a method, a level, a running algorithm, an internal transfer, and finally a value put on anything scarce.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个「标数」动作展开：卖方决定收多少，这个决定再被看作活动、体系、单项决策、方法、水平、持续运行的算法、内部转移，最后是为任何稀缺物标出的价值。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a price list rewritten so often that the pencil marks layer over one another.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张价目表被改得太频繁，铅笔痕迹层层叠起。

branches.en: ACT AND DECISION: the ongoing work, and one choice made inside it.
branches.cn: 活动与决策：持续进行的工作，以及其中的一项选择。

branches.en: THE SYSTEM: a whole schedule of charges taken as one arrangement.
branches.cn: 体系：把整张收费表当作一个安排。

branches.en: METHOD AND HEIGHT: how the number is reached, and how high it sits.
branches.cn: 方法与高度：数字如何算出，以及它处在多高。

branches.en: MACHINE AND GROUP: prices that move by the minute, and charges inside one company.
branches.cn: 机器与集团：按分钟变动的价格，以及一家公司内部的收费。

branches.en: ANYTHING SCARCE: the same act applied to time, risk or access.
branches.cn: 任何稀缺物：同一动作被用于时间、风险或准入。

intro.en: Pricing is a native action noun built on a Latin-derived noun, so one half is a borrowed root and the other a native suffix.
intro.cn: pricing 是建在拉丁来源名词上的本族动作名词，一半是借来的词根，另一半是本族后缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin pretium supplies price, precious and appraise; English -ing supplies pricing, selling and building.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 pretium 提供 price、precious 与 appraise；英语 -ing 提供 pricing、selling 与 building。

items.example: The Latin noun underlies several English words of worth.
items.exampleCN: 这个拉丁名词支撑着若干表示价值的英语词。

items.structure: Latin pretium via Old French pris
items.example: The price rose with the tariff.
Every item in the window is priced.
items.exampleCN: 橱窗里每件商品都标了价。

items.example: The repair was pricey but quick.
The letters are priceless to the family.
items.exampleCN: 这些信对这个家庭而言无价。

items.example: The launch was overpriced and stalled.
They underpriced the service to win users.
items.exampleCN: 他们把服务定价过低以争取用户。
一位专家为这栋房子估了价。

items.example: The metal is precious but common in the trade.
items.exampleCN: 这种金属很珍贵，但在业内很常见。

latinEntries.meaning: to value, set a price on

definition_zh: 阅读；读物；读数；解读；（议会）一读
definition_en: the act of interpreting written signs, the figure shown by an instrument, or a particular interpretation
core_image: 一只手翻过书页，另一只手指着仪表上刚刚停下的数字
scene: 他把温度计的读数记在纸上，又回到窗边的那本书里。 He wrote the reading from the thermometer on paper and went back to the book by the window.
sceneCN: 这里 reading 指仪表上的读数（第 2 个义项：仪表读数）；句意为他把温度计的读数记在纸上，又回到窗边的那本书里。

pos.zh: 阅读；读物；读数；解读；一读

senses.title: The act of reading
senses.definition: the activity of working through written marks and turning them into meaning
senses.definitionCN: 把书面符号一路读下去、变成意义的活动
senses.example: Her reading of the letter took less than a minute.
senses.exampleCN: 她读那封信用了不到一分钟。
senses.why: This is the plainest sense: an eye moving along a line until meaning appears.
senses.whyCN: 这是最朴素的一层：目光沿着一行走过去，直到意义浮现。

senses.title: A figure shown by an instrument
senses.definition: the value a gauge, meter or dial shows at a given moment
senses.definitionCN: 仪表、量器或表盘在某一刻显示出的数值
senses.example: The pressure reading had not moved since morning.
senses.exampleCN: 压力读数从早晨起就没有动过。
senses.why: Instruments write their sentences in numbers, and the word lends them the act of interpretation.
senses.whyCN: 仪表用数字写句子，这个词把「解读」这个动作借给了它们。

senses.title: An interpretation
senses.definition: a particular way of understanding a text, an event or a situation
senses.definitionCN: 对文本、事件或局势的一种特定理解
senses.example: Her reading of the novel stressed the silence, not the speeches.
senses.exampleCN: 她对这部小说的解读强调的是沉默，而不是那些演讲。
senses.why: The act becomes a position: readers can disagree, so a reading can be right or wrong.
senses.whyCN: 动作变成了立场：读者会争论，所以一种解读可能是对的，也可能是错的。

senses.title: A public recital
senses.definition: an event at which a text, often poems, is spoken aloud to an audience
senses.definitionCN: 把文本（常是诗）当众念给听众听的活动
senses.example: The poet gave a reading in a half-empty hall.
senses.exampleCN: 诗人在一个半空的大厅里做了一场朗诵。
senses.why: Here the noun names a gathering on a calendar rather than a private act.
senses.whyCN: 这里名词指的是日程表上的一场活动，而不是私下里的动作。

senses.title: Assigned texts
senses.definition: the set of books and articles a course or a group is asked to study
senses.definitionCN: 一门课或一个小组被要求研读的一批书与文章
senses.example: The syllabus listed readings in law, history and economics.
senses.exampleCN: 教学大纲列出了法律、历史与经济学方面的读本。
senses.why: The plural turns the activity into a bundle of texts with a deadline.
senses.whyCN: 复数把这项活动变成一捆带截止日期的文本。

intro.en: Reading is the noun from read, from Old English raedan, which meant to interpret, advise or reckon as well as to read.
intro.cn: reading 是 read 的名词形式，源自古英语 raedan，兼有解读、劝告、估算与阅读等义。

items.en: Raedan covered reading, advising and reckoning.
items.cn: raedan 兼指阅读、劝告与估算。

items.en: The noun named the act and what was read aloud.
items.cn: 这个名词指阅读行为，也指被朗读的内容。

items.en: Later the word was applied to what a gauge reads.
items.cn: 后来这个词被用于仪表所读出的数值。

items.en: Public libraries made readings a shared noun.
items.cn: 公共图书馆让 readings 成为共享的词。

items.en: Today it covers texts, data and interpretations alike.
items.cn: 今天它同时覆盖文本、数据与解读。

note.en: The look-alike group is the read- family; the near-meaning group separates interpretation, recitation, measurement and perusal.
note.cn: 形近组是 read 词族；近义组把「解释」「背诵」「测量」「细读」分开。

entries.definition: to interpret written marks.
entries.definitionCN: 解读书面符号。

entries.definition: a person who reads.
entries.definitionCN: 阅读的人。

entries.definition: easy to read.
entries.definitionCN: 容易读的。

entries.definition: a display of measured values.
entries.definitionCN: 测量数值的显示。

entries.definition: an explanation of meaning.
entries.definitionCN: 对含义的说明。

entries.definition: speaking a text from memory.
entries.definitionCN: 凭记忆背诵文本。

entries.definition: a size or amount obtained by measuring.
entries.definitionCN: 测量所得的尺寸或数量。

entries.definition: a careful reading through.
entries.definitionCN: 仔细通读。

normalIntro.en: The hooks keep the picture of one hand on a page and one hand on a dial.
normalIntro.cn: 以下联想留住「一只手在书页上，另一只手在表盘上」的画面。

normal.en: Reading is both an act and a number: the same word for two habits.
normal.cn: reading 既是动作也是数字：同一个词，两种习惯。

normal.en: Picture a thermometer and a book on the same desk.
normal.cn: 想象同一张桌上放着一支温度计和一本书。

normal.en: Say REE-ding; the word already sounds like a page turning.
normal.cn: 读 REE-ding，这个词本身就像翻页的声音。

normal.en: The plural readings usually means a set of texts or figures.
normal.cn: 复数 readings 通常指一套文本或一组数值。

normal.en: Ask which reading: of a bill, a gauge, a poem or a market?
normal.cn: 问是哪一种 reading：法案、仪表、诗，还是市场？

abstract.en: Reading is the point where the world is turned into signs and signs back into the world.
abstract.cn: reading 是世界变成符号、符号又变回世界的那个点。

abstract.en: Every instrument reading is a sentence the machine writes in numbers.
abstract.cn: 每一个仪表读数，都是机器用数字写下的一句话。

abstract.en: A reading of events is never neutral; it chooses what counts as evidence.
abstract.cn: 对事件的判断从不中性：它挑选什么算作证据。

examples.en: The pressure reading had not moved since morning.
examples.cn: 压力读数从早晨起就没有动过。

examples.en: Her reading of the novel stressed the silence, not the speeches.
examples.cn: 她对这部小说的解读强调的是沉默，而不是那些演讲。

examples.en: The bill failed at its second reading.
examples.cn: 这项法案在二读时失败了。

sensesIntro.en: Reading has five senses: the act, an instrument's figure, an interpretation, a public recital and the texts assigned to a course.
sensesIntro.cn: reading 有五层：阅读行为、仪表读数、解读、朗读会，以及课程指定的读本。

core.en: A PAGE AND A DIAL ON ONE DESK
core.cn: 一张桌上的书页与表盘

branches.en: The act itself and the position it produces.
branches.cn: 阅读行为本身，以及它产生的立场。

branches.en: Figures from a dial, texts from a syllabus.
branches.cn: 表盘上的数值，教学大纲上的文本。

branches.en: The word as a public event.
branches.cn: 作为公共活动的这个词。

branches.en: A number that stands in for a sentence.
branches.cn: 代替一句话的那个数字。

branches.en: Understanding set against performance.
branches.cn: 理解与表演相对。

intro.en: The read- family keeps one root: read, reader, reading and readout all describe turning marks into meaning or numbers.
intro.cn: read 词族共用一个根：read、reader、reading、readout 都描述把符号变成意义或数字。

latinIntro.en: Old English raedan supplies the verb; the -ing noun ending is Germanic, not Latin, and the word never needed a borrowed suffix.
latinIntro.cn: 古英语 raedan 提供动词；-ing 名词词尾属日耳曼语而非拉丁语，这个词从不需要借来的后缀。

items.meaning: the act or a figure read

latinEntries.meaning: to reckon, a distant cousin in sense
latinEntries.meaningCN: 估算，意义上的一位远亲

definition_zh: 唯美主义；审美崇拜；为艺术而艺术的主张
definition_en: the belief that art should be valued for beauty alone, especially the late nineteenth-century movement of art for art's sake
core_image: 一间把实用物件全部移走、只留下颜色与线条的房间
scene: 展厅里，导览说这批画家拒绝让画承担道德说教，只谈颜色与形状。 The guide explained that aestheticism rejected any moral duty for painting.
sceneCN: 这里 aestheticism 指「主张艺术只应追求美、不承担道德或实用任务的理论」（第 2 个义项：为艺术而艺术的信条）；句意为导览说明唯美主义拒绝让绘画承担道德义务。

pos.zh: 唯美主义；审美崇拜（通常不可数）

collocations.zh: 维多利亚时期的唯美主义
19 世纪 90 年代的唯美主义
为艺术而艺术的唯美主义

forms.label: 可数用法（少见，指多种形态）

derivatives.zh: 希腊 aisthētikos「可感知的」→ 审美的；从「感知」转到「美」
aesthetic + -ics（学问）→ 美学；从「性质」转到「学科」
aesthetic + -e（人）→ 审美者；从「性质」转到「以美为价值的人」
aestheticism + -ist（信奉者）→ 唯美主义者；从「主义」转到「持此主张的人」
aesthetic + -ize（使……化）→ 使带上审美色彩；从「性质」转到「施加动作」

senses.title: The late nineteenth-century movement
senses.titleCN: 19 世纪后期的唯美主义运动
senses.definition: the late Victorian movement that made beauty the chief aim of art and life
senses.definitionCN: 维多利亚后期把美作为艺术与生活首要目标的运动
senses.example: The novel is usually read as a document of aestheticism.
senses.exampleCN: 这部小说通常被读作唯美主义的一份文献。
senses.why: The suffix -ism names a movement as well as a doctrine, so aestheticism can denote the historical circle around Pater and Wilde.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -ism 既可命名主张，也可命名运动，因此 aestheticism 能指佩特与王尔德周围的那个历史圈子。

senses.title: Art for art's sake
senses.definition: the principle that art owes nothing to morality, utility or social purpose
senses.definitionCN: 艺术不对道德、实用或社会目的负有任何义务的原则
senses.example: Aestheticism holds that art owes no moral lesson.
senses.exampleCN: 唯美主义认为艺术不欠任何道德教训。
senses.why: The movement's core claim is that beauty is the only end of art; the name of the movement became the name of that claim.
senses.whyCN: 这场运动的核心主张是美是艺术的唯一目的；运动的名称于是成了这条主张的名称。

senses.title: Devotion to beauty as a value
senses.definition: a personal commitment to beauty as the highest good
senses.definitionCN: 把美视为最高善的个人承诺
senses.example: Her aestheticism extended to the arrangement of a dinner table.
senses.exampleCN: 她的唯美追求连餐桌的摆法都不放过。
senses.why: A doctrine can become a temperament: when someone lives by the primacy of beauty, the word describes the commitment rather than a movement.
senses.whyCN: 主张可以变成性情：当一个人按美的优先性生活，这个词描述的就是这种承诺，而不是一场运动。

senses.title: Life treated as a work of art
senses.definition: the attitude that experience itself should be shaped aesthetically
senses.definitionCN: 认为经验本身应按审美方式塑造的态度
senses.example: Pater's aestheticism treated life itself as a work of art.
senses.exampleCN: 佩特的唯美主义把生活本身当作艺术品。
senses.why: If art needs no purpose outside beauty, then a life can be composed like an artwork; the doctrine extends from objects to conduct.
senses.whyCN: 如果艺术在美之外无需目的，那么生活也可以像艺术品一样被经营；主张因此从物件扩展到行为。

senses.title: A decorative style
senses.definition: the visual style associated with the aesthetic movement, especially in interiors and dress
senses.definitionCN: 与唯美运动相关的视觉风格，尤见于室内与服饰
senses.example: The house is a monument of eighteen-nineties aestheticism.
senses.exampleCN: 这座房子是 19 世纪 90 年代唯美主义风格的纪念碑。
senses.why: A movement leaves objects behind; its characteristic palette and patterns come to be called by the movement's name.
senses.whyCN: 运动会在物件上留下痕迹；其特有的色彩与纹样便被以运动之名相称。

senses.title: Over-concern with appearance
senses.titleCN: 对外观的过度讲究（贬义）
senses.definition: a pejorative term for excessive attention to surface beauty
senses.definitionCN: 贬义用法，指对表面之美的过度关注
senses.example: Critics attacked the aestheticism of the campaign as mere decoration.
senses.exampleCN: 批评者抨击这场宣传活动只是装饰性的唯美做派。
senses.why: Any value can be mocked when it looks like evasion; aestheticism became a label for prettiness that avoids harder questions.
senses.whyCN: 任何价值在被视为逃避时都可能被讥讽；aestheticism 成了「只顾好看、回避难题」的标签。

senses.title: A stance in literary criticism
senses.titleCN: 文学批评中的一种立场
senses.definition: an approach that judges literature by formal beauty rather than moral or social effect
senses.definitionCN: 按形式之美而非道德或社会效果来评判文学的路径
senses.example: His aestheticism shaped a generation of literary criticism.
senses.exampleCN: 他的唯美立场塑造了一代文学批评。
senses.why: Literary criticism borrowed the movement's name for a method: reading for form, texture and pleasure rather than message.
senses.whyCN: 文学批评借用了这场运动的名字来命名一种方法：为形式、质感与愉悦而读，而非为信息而读。

senses.title: Beauty as the chief criterion in a field
senses.titleCN: 某一领域以美为主要标准
senses.definition: the tendency to put aesthetic appeal first in a domain outside art
senses.definitionCN: 在艺术之外的领域中把审美吸引力放在首位的倾向
senses.example: The brand's aestheticism puts beauty ahead of function.
senses.exampleCN: 这个品牌的唯美取向把美观放在功能之前。
senses.why: The doctrine's single criterion can be imported anywhere, so design, advertising or even engineering may be charged with aestheticism.
senses.whyCN: 这条主张的唯一标准可以被输入任何领域，因此设计、广告甚至工程都可能被指为唯美主义。

intro.en: Aestheticism is a nineteenth-century English formation: aesthetic plus -ism, recorded in 1855 and later tied to the art-for-art's-sake circle. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: aestheticism 是 19 世纪英语构词：aesthetic 加 -ism，1855 年有记录，后来与「为艺术而艺术」的圈子联系在一起。年代均为约数。

items.en: Aisthēsis 'perception' supplied the root of aesthetic; the sensory meaning is older than the meaning 'beautiful'.
items.cn: aisthēsis「感知」提供 aesthetic 的词根；感官义比「美」义更早。

items.en: Baumgarten's eighteenth-century coinage made aesthetics a name for the science of sensory knowledge.
items.cn: 鲍姆加登 18 世纪的造词使 aesthetics 成为感官知识之学的名称。

items.en: English aesthetic appeared in 1798; by the 1830s it commonly meant the appreciation of beauty.
items.cn: 英语 aesthetic 于 1798 年出现；到 1830 年代，它通常指对美的欣赏。

items.en: The suffix -ism, from Greek -ismos through Latin -ismus, names a practice, doctrine or movement.
items.cn: 后缀 -ism 经拉丁 -ismus 来自希腊 -ismos，命名一种实践、主张或运动。

items.en: Aestheticism is recorded in 1855 in the sense 'devotion to what is sensuously beautiful'.
items.cn: aestheticism 于 1855 年有记录，意为「对感官之美的献身」。

items.en: Later in the century the word was attached to Pater, Wilde and the art-for-art's-sake programme, and that historical sense now leads.
items.cn: 到该世纪后期，这个词与佩特、王尔德及「为艺术而艺术」纲领联系在一起，这一历史义如今最突出。

note.en: Group one separates aestheticism from the aisth- words it is built on; group two separates it from neighbouring movements and doctrines of art.
note.cn: 第一组把 aestheticism 与它所由来的 aisth- 词分开；第二组把它与邻近的艺术运动与主张分开。

entries.definition: A quality or principle of beauty; aestheticism is the doctrine that makes beauty supreme.
entries.definitionCN: 美的性质或原则；aestheticism 是把美置于至高位置的主张。

entries.definition: The philosophical study of beauty and art; it can analyse aestheticism without adopting it.
entries.definitionCN: 研究美与艺术的哲学；它可以分析唯美主义而不采纳它。

entries.definition: A devotee of beauty; aestheticism is the creed such a person may hold.
entries.definitionCN: 美的崇拜者；aestheticism 是此人可能持有的信条。

entries.definition: Loss of sensation; it shares the perceptual root but has no connection with the art movement.
entries.definitionCN: 感觉丧失；同出感知词根，但与这场艺术运动无关。

entries.definition: The French-derived phrase l'art pour l'art, translated in 1824; it is the slogan of aestheticism rather than its name.
entries.definitionCN: 源自法语 l'art pour l'art，1824 年有英译；它是唯美主义的口号，而不是其名称。

entries.definition: A late nineteenth-century literary mood of refinement and decline; it overlaps with aestheticism but adds exhaustion and perversity.
entries.definitionCN: 19 世纪后期的文学情绪，讲究精致与衰颓；与唯美主义重叠，但多了疲惫与乖僻。

entries.definition: The critical priority of formal structure over content; aestheticism is broader and adds a doctrine about beauty's value.
entries.definitionCN: 批评上把形式结构置于内容之上；aestheticism 更广，并附加关于美之价值的主张。

entries.definition: The cultivation of an elegant, conspicuous self-presentation; it is a social cousin of aestheticism, not the same programme.
entries.definitionCN: 对优雅而惹眼的自我呈现的经营；是唯美主义的社会近亲，而非同一纲领。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real compounds and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: aesthetic + -ism: the doctrine that beauty is the point.
normal.cn: aesthetic + -ism：以美为要旨的主张。

normal.en: -ism names movements as well as beliefs, so the word covers both a creed and a circle.
normal.cn: -ism 既命名主张也命名运动，因此这个词既指信条也指圈子。

normal.en: Fixed phrases date it: Victorian aestheticism, the aestheticism of the eighteen-nineties.
normal.cn: 固定搭配为它标年代：维多利亚唯美主义、19 世纪 90 年代的唯美主义。

normal.en: The family runs aesthetic, aesthetics, aesthete, aestheticism and aestheticist.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 aesthetic、aesthetics、aesthete、aestheticism 与 aestheticist。

normal.en: The slogan art for art's sake translates French l'art pour l'art, recorded in English in 1824.
normal.cn: 口号「为艺术而艺术」译自法语 l'art pour l'art，英语 1824 年有记录。

abstract.en: Picture a room with every useful object removed and only colour left.
abstract.cn: 想象一个房间，实用物件全被移走，只剩下颜色。

abstract.en: Picture a frame that refuses to hold anything but the surface it shows.
abstract.cn: 想象一个画框，只肯装它展示的那层表面。

abstract.en: Picture a life arranged with the same care as a shelf of porcelain.
abstract.cn: 想象一段生活被安排得像一柜瓷器那样精心。

examples.en: Aestheticism is often taught through the trial of Oscar Wilde.
examples.cn: 唯美主义常通过王尔德的审判来讲授。

examples.en: The movement's aestheticism did not deny politics; it refused to let politics judge art.
examples.cn: 这场运动的唯美主义并不否认政治，而是拒绝让政治评判艺术。

examples.en: Modern branding repeats the aestheticism of the eighteen-nineties in a commercial key.
examples.cn: 现代品牌以商业调子重复着 19 世纪 90 年代的唯美主义。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「aesthetic（审美的）+ -ism（主义）」——审美至上主义 → 唯美主义

root: aesthetic 来自希腊 aisthētikos「可感知的」，词根 aisthēsis「感知」；-ism 经拉丁 -ismus 来自希腊 -ismos，命名主张或运动。aestheticism 于 1855 年出现。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from the historical movement to its doctrine, then to a personal creed, a way of life, a decorative style, a pejorative label, a critical method and finally a general criterion outside art.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从历史运动转到其主张，再到个人信条、生活方式、装饰风格、贬义标签、批评方法，最后落到艺术之外的普遍标准。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a room emptied of useful things, where only colour and line remain.
core.cn: 核心意象：一间移走实用物件、只留下颜色与线条的房间。

branches.en: THE MOVEMENT AND ITS CRITERION: a historical circle, then the same priority applied anywhere.
branches.cn: 运动及其标准：先是一个历史圈子，再是同一优先性被用到任何领域。

branches.en: THE DOCTRINE AND THE METHOD: art owes no moral lesson, and criticism reads for form.
branches.cn: 主张与方法：艺术不欠道德教训，批评则为形式而读。

branches.en: A CREED LIVED: devotion to beauty becomes a way of composing experience.
branches.cn: 被实践的信条：对美的献身变成安排经验的方式。

branches.en: A STYLE LEFT BEHIND: the movement survives in palettes, patterns and interiors.
branches.cn: 留下的风格：运动在色彩、纹样与室内中继续存在。

branches.en: THE MOCKING NAME: concern with surface becomes a charge of evasion.
branches.cn: 被讥讽之名：对表面的关注被指控为逃避。

intro.en: Aestheticism is a Greek root plus two suffixes, one making an adjective and one making a doctrine, so the whole word can be read in layers.
intro.cn: aestheticism 是希腊词根加两个后缀，一个构成形容词，一个构成主张，因此整个词可以分层读出。

latinIntro.en: The root is Greek, not Latin; Latin contributes only the shape of the suffix -ismus, which English took through French -isme.
latinIntro.cn: 词根是希腊语而非拉丁语；拉丁语只提供后缀 -ismus 的形状，英语经法语 -isme 取得。

items.example: The root begins the whole family.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根开启整个词族。

items.example: The suffix makes aesthetic an adjective.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀使 aesthetic 成为形容词。

items.example: Realism and formalism use the same suffix.
items.exampleCN: realism 与 formalism 用的是同一个后缀。

items.meaning: the doctrine of beauty for its own sake
items.exampleCN: 唯美主义拒绝道德训诫。

items.example: The aestheticist wrote only about surfaces.
items.exampleCN: 这位唯美主义者只写表面。
这部影片把工厂审美化了。

items.meaning: from an aesthetic point of view
items.exampleCN: 这条街在审美上是一致的。
美学可以冷静地研究唯美主义。

definition_zh: 形容词：巴洛克风格的（十七世纪繁复华丽）；过度雕琢的。名词：巴洛克风格；巴洛克时期（音乐约1600至1750）
definition_en: of the ornate seventeenth-century style in art and music; the style or period itself; excessively ornate or convoluted
core_image: 一颗长歪的珍珠，和一片堆满金饰曲线的顶棚
scene: 教堂顶棚满是金饰与曲线，导游说这是十七世纪的手笔。 The ceiling is baroque, all curves and gold leaf.
sceneCN: 这里 baroque 是「巴洛克风格的」（第 1 个义项：十七世纪那种繁复华丽的艺术风格）；句意是这顶棚是巴洛克式的，满是曲线与金箔。

pos.zh: 形容词：巴洛克风格的；繁复矫饰的
名词：巴洛克风格；巴洛克时期

collocations.zh: 巴洛克小提琴（古乐演奏）

forms.label: 形容词原级（无屈折变化）

derivatives.zh: 形容词：洛可可式的，巴洛克之后的纤巧风格
名词：风格主义，巴洛克之前的手法主义

senses.title: The ornate style
senses.definition: of the elaborate, dramatic style of seventeenth-century art and architecture
senses.definitionCN: 属于十七世纪艺术与建筑那种繁复而富戏剧性的风格
senses.example: The ceiling is baroque, all curves and gold leaf.
senses.exampleCN: 这顶棚是巴洛克式的，满是曲线与金箔。
senses.why: French baroque meant bizarre; critics turned the insult into a style label.
senses.whyCN: 法语 baroque 本指「怪异」；批评家把这个贬称变成了风格标签。

senses.title: The music period
senses.definition: the period of European music from about 1600 to 1750
senses.definitionCN: 约 1600 至 1750 年的欧洲音乐时期
senses.example: They played baroque music on gut-strung violins.
senses.exampleCN: 他们用羊肠弦小提琴演奏巴洛克音乐。
senses.why: The style label was extended to the whole age that produced it.
senses.whyCN: 风格标签被扩展到产生它的整个时代。

senses.title: The style as a noun
senses.definition: the baroque style or period itself, used as a noun
senses.definitionCN: 巴洛克风格或时期本身，用作名词
senses.example: The palace is a textbook example of the baroque.
senses.exampleCN: 这座宫殿是巴洛克风格的教科书式范例。
senses.why: English lets the adjective stand as a noun with no ending added.
senses.whyCN: 英语允许形容词不加词尾直接作名词。

senses.title: Overdone and convoluted
senses.definition: excessively ornate, elaborate or tangled in style
senses.definitionCN: 风格上过度雕琢、繁复或纠缠不清
senses.example: His baroque prose hid a very simple argument.
senses.exampleCN: 他那繁复矫饰的文风掩盖了一个极简单的论点。
senses.why: A crooked pearl became a metaphor for anything twisted out of proportion.
senses.whyCN: 歪珍珠成了比喻，指任何扭曲失度的东西。

senses.title: Historical performance
senses.definition: in baroque violin or baroque pitch, the instruments and tuning of that age

intro.en: Baroque starts as a crooked pearl and ends as a style with too much gold on it.
intro.cn: baroque 从一颗歪珍珠出发，最后变成堆满金饰的风格。

items.en: Baroco was the medieval mnemonic for a convoluted syllogism; some trace the pearl word to it.
items.cn: Baroco 是中世纪逻辑学里一个绕口三段论的助记名；有人把「歪珠」一词追溯到它。

items.en: Portuguese barroco named an irregular, misshapen pearl.
items.cn: 葡萄牙语 barroco 指形状不规则的歪珍珠。

items.en: French baroque meant irregular, then bizarre or over-ornate.
items.cn: 法语 baroque 先指「不规则」，后指「怪异、过度装饰」。

items.en: English took it for odd, extravagantly decorated taste.
items.cn: 英语借入，指趣味怪诞、装饰过度。

items.en: Critics named the ornate seventeenth-century style baroque.
items.cn: 艺术史家把十七世纪那种繁复风格命名为巴洛克。

items.en: Today it is a period noun and an adjective for anything overdone.
items.cn: 今天它既是时期名词，也形容任何过度雕琢之物。

note.en: The look-alike group shares bar-; the near-meaning group lists neighbouring styles and words for excess.
note.cn: 形近组共享 bar-；近义组列出相邻风格与表示「过度」的词。

normalIntro.en: Baroque names a crooked pearl first, then a century of gilded curves.

normal.en: The music period runs roughly from 1600 to 1750.

normal.en: As an adjective it can praise or blame: ornate, or overdone.
normal.cn: 作形容词可褒可贬：华丽，或过度雕琢。

normal.en: Rococo follows baroque and is lighter and more playful.

examples.en: They played baroque music on gut-strung violins.
examples.cn: 他们用羊肠弦小提琴演奏巴洛克音乐。

examples.en: His baroque prose hid a very simple argument.
examples.cn: 他那繁复矫饰的文风掩盖了一个极简单的论点。

dict_mnemonic.text: 葡萄牙语 barroco「不规则的珍珠」到法语 baroque「怪异」，再到十七世纪那种堆满曲线与金饰的风格；珍珠歪了叫 baroque，文章绕了也叫 baroque。

root: 源自葡萄牙语 barroco「形状不规则的珍珠」，经法语 baroque「怪异、不规则」进入英语；十八世纪指趣味怪诞，十九世纪被艺术史家用来命名十七世纪那种繁复华丽的风格，再引申为「过度雕琢的」。

definition_zh: 振动；颤动；（地面或建筑传来的）震动；（口语）氛围、气场；振动能
definition_en: a rapid movement back and forth about a fixed point, or the shaking and energy that such movement produces
core_image: 一根被拨动的琴弦在两个极限位置之间来回，留下残影般的一道弧线
scene: 音乐教室的午后，老师把音叉敲响后，将柄端抵在木桌边缘，桌上的纸片轻轻跳起。 A faint vibration passes through the table and makes the paper slip.
sceneCN: 这里 vibration 是名词「通过固体传导的震动」（第 3 个义项：地面或建筑结构接收并传递的振动）；句意为一次微弱的振动穿过桌面，使纸片滑了一下。

pos.zh: 振动；颤动；传导的震动；（口语）氛围、气场；振动能

derivatives.zh: 充满生气的；鲜明的；（声音）洪亮的

senses.title: Rapid back-and-forth motion
senses.definition: a rapid alternation of position about a rest point, as of a pendulum, a string or a membrane
senses.definitionCN: 围绕静止位置快速交替位移，如摆、弦或膜的运动
senses.example: The vibration of the plucked string dies away within a second.
senses.exampleCN: 被拨动的琴弦一秒内就停止了振动。
senses.why: Latin vibrare meant to move quickly to and fro, so the noun names the pattern itself before it names any particular object that shakes.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 vibrare 意为快速来回移动，因此这个名词先指运动模式本身，而非某个具体的抖动之物。

senses.title: Mechanical vibration
senses.definition: the shaking of a machine, engine or structure during normal running or because of wear
senses.definitionCN: 机器、发动机或结构在正常运转中或因磨损而产生的抖动
senses.example: Engineers track vibration in the gearbox as an early sign of wear.
senses.exampleCN: 工程师监测齿轮箱的振动，把它当作磨损的早期信号。
senses.why: industry needed a measurable name for unwanted shaking, and the general physical noun supplied it without metaphor.
senses.whyCN: 工业需要一个可测量的词来指不受欢迎的抖动，这个一般物理名词无需比喻就提供了它。

senses.title: Shaking transmitted through a solid
senses.definition: movement or shaking that passes through the ground, a floor or a building from a distant source
senses.definitionCN: 由远处震源传来、穿过地面、楼板或建筑结构的运动或抖动
senses.example: Passing trucks send vibration through the old brick wall.
senses.exampleCN: 过路的卡车把振动传过老砖墙。
senses.why: the physical sense easily extends from the object that shakes to the path along which the shaking travels.
senses.whyCN: 这个物理义很容易从「抖动的物体」扩展到「抖动传播所经过的路径」。

senses.title: Vibration of strings and vocal cords
senses.definition: the rapid oscillation of a stretched string or of the vocal folds that produces sound
senses.definitionCN: 张紧的弦或声带快速振荡并由此产生声音
senses.example: The vocal cords produce sound through rapid vibration.
senses.exampleCN: 声带通过快速振动发出声音。
senses.why: sound is literally vibration in air, so acoustics uses the same word for the source and for what reaches the ear.
senses.whyCN: 声音本来就是空气的振动，所以声学用同一个词既指声源，也指传到耳朵的东西。

senses.title: Frequency and amplitude
senses.definition: the measurable rate and size of a vibration, usually given in cycles per second and in displacement
senses.definitionCN: 振动可测量的快慢与幅度，通常以每秒周期数和位移来表示
senses.example: The device records vibration at two frequencies at once.
senses.exampleCN: 该装置同时记录两个频率上的振动。
senses.why: once vibration became an engineering quantity, it needed numbers: how often it repeats and how far it moves.
senses.whyCN: 一旦振动成为工程量，就需要数字：它重复得多快，以及移动得多远。

senses.title: Isolation and damping
senses.definition: the engineering practice of reducing unwanted vibration before it reaches people, instruments or buildings
senses.definitionCN: 在不受欢迎的振动传到人、仪器或建筑之前削减它的工程做法
senses.example: Rubber mounts provide vibration isolation for the sensitive microscope.
senses.exampleCN: 橡胶支座为敏感显微镜提供隔振。
senses.why: the noun can stand for the thing being controlled, as in isolation and damping, because the problem and its remedy share one name.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词可以指被控制的对象，如隔振与阻尼，因为问题与对策共用同一个名称。

senses.title: Atmosphere or emotional quality
senses.definition: an emotional quality felt in a place, a group or a piece of music, often used in the plural
senses.definitionCN: 某地、某群体或某段音乐给人的情绪感受，常用复数
senses.example: The room had good vibrations that put everyone at ease.
senses.exampleCN: 那个房间有一种让人放松的良好氛围。
senses.why: the sixties turned the physical word into slang for a felt atmosphere, as if mood were something transmitted through a room.
senses.whyCN: 二十世纪六十年代把这一物理词变成指可感氛围的俚语，仿佛情绪也能在房间里传播。

senses.title: Vibrational energy
senses.definition: the energy carried by an oscillating system, counted in physics as part of its internal energy
senses.definitionCN: 振荡系统所携带的能量，物理学上计为其内能的一部分
senses.example: The sensor converts vibration into electrical current.
senses.exampleCN: 传感器把振动能转换成电流。
senses.why: physics treats vibration as a form of energy, so the noun can name the quantity that a device harvests.
senses.whyCN: 物理学把振动视为一种能量，因此这个名词也能指装置所收集的那个量。

intro.en: Vibration comes from Latin vibratio, a shaking or brandishing, built on the verb vibrare. English took the noun in the seventeenth century, and acoustics and engineering later gave it measured frequency and amplitude.
intro.cn: vibration 来自拉丁 vibratio「摇动、挥舞」，建于动词 vibrare 之上。英语于十七世纪借入这个名词，声学与工程后来给它加上了可测的频率与振幅。

items.en: Vibrare meant to move rapidly to and fro, to brandish or wave a weapon, and also to quiver. It is the single verb behind the whole English family.
items.cn: vibrare 意为快速来回移动、挥舞武器，也指抖动。整个英语同族词都出自这一个动词。

items.en: Vibratio was the noun of action, a shaking or a waving, formed with the same -tio suffix seen in many Latin action nouns.
items.cn: vibratio 是动作名词，指摇动或挥舞，用与许多拉丁动作名词相同的 -tio 后缀构成。

items.en: The perfect participle vibratus, having been shaken, supplied the stem vibrat- that passed through French into English vibration.
items.cn: 完成分词 vibratus 意为「已被摇动」，提供了经法语进入英语 vibration 的词干 vibrat-。

items.en: Vibrato is an Italian borrowing from the same Latin root, naming a rapid fluctuation of pitch in singing or playing. It is a cousin of vibration, not a child of it.
items.cn: vibrato 是从同一拉丁词根借入意大利语的词，指歌唱或演奏中音高的快速起伏。它是 vibration 的同族表亲，而非其派生词。

items.en: English vibration is generally dated to the seventeenth century as a word for shaking; the modern technical senses of frequency, amplitude and isolation belong to later physics and engineering.
items.cn: 英语 vibration 一般被认为是十七世纪表示「摇动」的词；频率、振幅与隔振等现代技术义属于后来的物理学与工程学。

items.en: Two tiers of doubt: the first date of the technical senses is approximate, a dating question; the deeper root of vibrare is usually linked to a reconstructed Indo-European word for quivering, but that link is a reconstruction, not a recorded form, a root question.
items.cn: 来源不确定，分两档：技术义的首见年代只是约数，属年代存疑；vibrare 更深的词根通常被联系到一个重构的印欧语「抖动」词，但这一联系属于重构，并非有记录的形式，属词根存疑。

note.en: Group one holds words from the same Latin shaking stock; group two holds near neighbours for motion, sound and felt atmosphere.
note.cn: 第一组是同出拉丁「摇动」词干的词；第二组是表示运动、声音与可感氛围的近义词。

entries.definition: To move rapidly back and forth, or to cause something to do so; it is the action behind every noun sense of vibration.
entries.definitionCN: 快速来回运动，或使某物如此运动；它是 vibration 各名词义背后的动作。

entries.definition: Full of life, color or sound, literally vibrating; the physical sense survives in descriptions of rich color and strong voices.
entries.definitionCN: 充满生气、色彩或声音的，字面义为「正在振动」；其物理义仍残留在对浓烈色彩与洪亮嗓音的描写中。

entries.definition: A controlled, rapid variation in pitch in music; it shares the Latin root but reached English through Italian, not through the noun vibration.
entries.definitionCN: 音乐中受控的快速音高变化；它与本词共享拉丁词根，但经意大利语进入英语，而非由 vibration 派生。

entries.definition: The quality of being vibrant: liveliness of color, sound or personality, with the physical shaking faded into metaphor.
entries.definitionCN: 「有活力」的性质：色彩、声音或个性的鲜活，其中的物理抖动已淡化为比喻。

entries.definition: A fine shaking, especially of the body or the ground; unlike vibration it usually suggests something unwanted or uncontrollable.
entries.definitionCN: 细密的抖动，尤其指身体或地面；与 vibration 不同，它通常暗示不受欢迎或无法控制。

entries.definition: A regular swinging from one side to the other, often slower and more orderly than vibration.
entries.definitionCN: 有规律地从一侧摆到另一侧，通常比振动更慢、更有秩序。

entries.definition: The general act of moving something quickly up and down or side to side; vibration is its technical, repetitive counterpart.
entries.definitionCN: 使某物快速上下或左右移动的一般动作；vibration 是它技术化、重复化的对应词。

entries.definition: The strong response of a system when it is driven at its natural frequency, producing a much larger vibration.
entries.definitionCN: 系统在固有频率被驱动时产生的强烈响应，会形成大得多的振动。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real Latin stem, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的拉丁词干、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: vibr- is the shaking stem: Latin vibrare waved and quivered, and vibration is the pattern it leaves.
normal.cn: vibr- 是「摇动」的词干：拉丁 vibrare 是挥舞与抖动，vibration 是它留下的运动模式。

normal.en: The family splits by part of speech: a verb, an adjective, a noun of quality and a musical noun.
normal.cn: 同族按词性分流：一个动词、一个形容词、一个表性质的抽象名词与一个音乐名词。

normal.en: Frequency and amplitude are the two numbers engineers give a vibration.
normal.cn: 频率与振幅是工程师描述一次振动时给出的两个数字。

normal.en: The plural turns physical: good vibrations is about mood, not machinery.
normal.cn: 复数形式转向心理：所谓「良好的氛围」说的是情绪，而非机器。

normal.en: Isolation and damping are the practical side: stop the vibration before it arrives.
normal.cn: 隔振与阻尼是实用的一面：在振动到达之前就拦住它。

abstract.en: Picture a guitar string blurred into a fan shape while it sounds.
abstract.cn: 想象一根吉他弦发声时模糊成扇形的一道残影。

abstract.en: Picture a wine glass singing until the note turns dangerous.
abstract.cn: 想象一只酒杯一直鸣响，直到那个音变得危险。

abstract.en: Picture a room whose mood changes the moment one person walks in.
abstract.cn: 想象一间屋子，某个人一走进来，气氛立刻变了。

examples.en: The bridge was closed after sensors detected unusual vibration in one span.
examples.cn: 传感器在一跨桥段检测到异常振动后，大桥被关闭。

examples.en: He felt the vibration of the train long before it appeared.
examples.cn: 火车还没出现，他就感到了它的振动。

examples.en: Rubber pads reduce the vibration that reaches the microscope.
examples.cn: 橡胶垫减少了传到显微镜的振动。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「vibr（摇摆）+ ation」——像琴弦来回摆动 → 振动、颤动、氛围气场

root: 拉丁 vibrare「快速来回移动、挥动」的动名词 vibratio「摇动」；同族有动词「振动」、形容词「鲜明的、有活力的」与意大利语借词「颤音」，另有名词「振动器」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one pattern: something moves back and forth around a rest point. The pattern is first named in itself, then located in machines, buildings, strings and voices, measured, controlled, and finally read as mood or as energy.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一种模式展开：某物围绕静止位置来回运动。这个模式先被命名，再依次落到机器、建筑、琴弦与声音上，被测量、被控制，最后被读成氛围或能量。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a taut string swinging between two extremes and never resting at the middle.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根绷紧的弦在两个极端之间来回，从不在中间停留。

branches.en: MOTION ITSELF: the bare physical pattern, before any object or use is attached.
branches.cn: 运动本身：尚未附上任何物体或用途的纯粹物理模式。

branches.en: MACHINE AND CONTROL: shaking as a symptom to be watched and then reduced.
branches.cn: 机器与控制：抖动先是需要监测的症状，随后被削减。

branches.en: STRUCTURE: the same shaking travels through ground, floor and wall.
branches.cn: 结构：同一种抖动穿过地面、楼板与墙体。

branches.en: SOUND AND MEASURE: strings and vocal folds make it audible, instruments make it countable.
branches.cn: 声音与测量：琴弦与声带让它被听见，仪器让它可计数。

branches.en: MOOD AND ENERGY: the pattern is felt as atmosphere or harvested as power.
branches.cn: 氛围与能量：这种模式或被感受为气氛，或被收集为能量。

intro.en: Vibration is a Latin action noun built from a verb stem plus a suffix, with the same stem surviving in a verb, two adjectives and an Italian musical borrowing.
intro.cn: vibration 是由动词词干加后缀构成的拉丁动作名词，同一词干还留存在一个动词、两个形容词与一个意大利语音乐借词中。

latinIntro.en: Latin vibrare, vibratio and vibratus feed vibration, vibrate, vibrant and vibrato.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 vibrare、vibratio 与 vibratus 衍生出本词及「振动」「有活力的」「颤音」等同族词。

items.example: The stem vibr- carries the swinging motion.
items.exampleCN: 词干 vibr- 承载来回摆动的动作。

items.meaning: the act or state of doing
items.example: Vibration is the state of being shaken.
items.exampleCN: 该名词指「被摇动」的状态。

items.example: The vibration was measured at fifty cycles per second.
items.exampleCN: 测得的振动为每秒五十个周期。

items.example: The phone vibrates on the desk.
The market was vibrant with color and noise.
items.exampleCN: 市场色彩鲜明、人声鼎沸。

items.example: The vibrancy of the paint surprised the curator.
items.exampleCN: 颜料的鲜亮让策展人吃惊。

items.example: The violinist added vibrato to the slow passage.
items.exampleCN: 小提琴手在缓慢的乐段里加了颤音。

items.example: A small vibrator tested the loose connection.
items.exampleCN: 一个小振动器测试了松动的接头。

items.example: The spectrum shows vibrational energy levels.

definition_zh: 贵族的；贵族出身的；贵族式的；高傲的
definition_en: belonging to or characteristic of a noble class, especially in manner, taste or bearing
core_image: 一个年轻人站在老宅的石阶上，背挺得很直，说话很慢，却从不动手做事
scene: 来人宁可站着等半小时，也不肯自己去搬那把椅子。 He had an aristocratic dislike of anything that looked like effort.
sceneCN: 这里 aristocratic 指贵族式的、带着阶层习气与傲气的（第 2 个义项：贵族式的风度）；句意为他对一切看上去像出力的东西都有一种贵族式的厌恶。

pos.zh: 贵族的；贵族出身的；贵族式的

derivatives.zh: 贵族阶层（aristocratic 去后缀，由属性转指持有它的阶层）
贵族（aristocracy + -crat「成员」，由阶层转指其中一员）
以贵族方式（aristocratic + -ally，由属性转指方式）
贵族作风（少见派生，aristocratic + -ism，由属性转指作风体系）

senses.title: Of noble birth
senses.definition: born into a family holding inherited title, land or rank
senses.definitionCN: 出生于世袭持有头衔、土地或等级的家族
senses.example: Her aristocratic origins opened doors that money could not.
senses.exampleCN: 她的贵族出身打开了钱打不开的门。
senses.why: the adjective attaches the class to a person, and birth is the oldest marker of that class.
senses.whyCN: 形容词把阶层接到人身上，而出身是这一阶层最古老的标记。

senses.title: In noble manner
senses.definition: carrying oneself with the reserve and assurance associated with the class
senses.definitionCN: 带着与该阶层相关的克制与笃定行事
senses.example: He had an aristocratic dislike of anything that looked like effort.
senses.exampleCN: 他对一切看上去像出力的东西都有一种贵族式的厌恶。
senses.why: manner outlives title, so the adjective often describes bearing rather than a pedigree.
senses.whyCN: 风度比头衔活得久，因此形容词常描述举止而非家谱。

senses.title: Of noble rule
senses.definition: concerning government by a hereditary elite
senses.definitionCN: 关于由世袭精英统治
senses.example: The aristocratic constitution gave the upper chamber a veto.
senses.exampleCN: 贵族政制给上院一票否决权。
senses.why: the political sense survives in constitutional history, where forms rather than families are at issue.
senses.whyCN: 政治义存于宪制史中，那里讨论的是形式而非家族。

senses.title: Haughty
senses.definition: showing a superior air that expects deference
senses.definitionCN: 显出期待他人退让的优越姿态
senses.example: His aristocratic shrug ended the conversation.
senses.exampleCN: 他那个贵族式的耸肩结束了谈话。
senses.why: the manner becomes a vice when the assurance turns into contempt.
senses.whyCN: 当笃定转为轻蔑，风度就成了一种毛病。

senses.title: Of noble taste
senses.definition: showing the cultivated preferences historically cultivated by the class
senses.definitionCN: 显出历史上由该阶层培养出的偏好
senses.example: The collection reflects aristocratic taste in furniture.
senses.exampleCN: 这批藏品反映了贵族在家具上的品味。
senses.why: leisure and inheritance produced a style that later spreads far beyond the class.
senses.whyCN: 闲暇与继承造就一种风格，这种风格后来远播阶层之外。

senses.title: Of an upper social layer
senses.definition: belonging to the top layer of a local society, titled or not
senses.definitionCN: 属于某地社会的顶层，无论有无头衔
senses.example: The town's aristocratic set met on the same veranda each summer.
senses.exampleCN: 镇上的上流圈子每年夏天都在同一个游廊聚会。
senses.why: in small places the class is defined socially rather than legally, and the adjective follows.
senses.whyCN: 在小地方，阶层由社交而非法律界定，形容词也随之。

senses.title: Exclusive in spirit
senses.definition: reserved for a closed circle and cold to outsiders
senses.definitionCN: 只对封闭圈子开放，对外人冷淡
senses.example: The club kept an aristocratic membership rule for a century.
senses.exampleCN: 该俱乐部维持了一个世纪的排他入会规则。
senses.why: exclusiveness is the social mechanism that keeps the class a class.
senses.whyCN: 排他性是使这一阶层成其为阶层的社交机制。

senses.title: Of a cultural elite
senses.titleCN: 文化精英的、精英主义的
senses.definition: marking a claim to superior standards in art or letters, without any title
senses.definitionCN: 在艺术或文学上主张更高标准，却无任何头衔
senses.example: The journal's aristocratic tone kept younger writers out.
senses.exampleCN: 这份刊物的精英腔调把年轻作者挡在门外。
senses.why: the word can describe anyone who borrows the class's authority over standards.
senses.whyCN: 任何借用该阶层对标准之权威的人，都能被这个词描述。

intro.en: Aristocratic is aristocracy plus -ic, from Greek aristos 'best' and kratos 'power', passed through French. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: aristocratic 是 aristocracy 加 -ic，来自希腊 aristos「最优」与 kratos「力量」，经法语传入。年代均为约数。

items.en: Aristos 'best' was the superlative of agathos; its internal formation is not fully explained and older segmentations are hypotheses.
items.cn: aristos「最优」是 agathos 的最高级；其内部构成未获完整解释，较早的切分办法均属假说。

items.en: Aristokratia named a constitution in which the best citizens ruled, a term of political theory before it named a class.
items.cn: aristokratia 指最优公民统治的政体，在指阶层之前是政治理论的术语。

items.en: French supplied the adjective, and English took it in the eighteenth century as noble families became a social rather than a ruling body.
items.cn: 法语提供形容词，英语在 18 世纪借入，正值贵族家族成为社会群体而非统治机构。

items.en: In the nineteenth century the adjective spread from birth to bearing, taste and disdain, describing a style anyone might imitate.
items.cn: 19 世纪这个形容词从出身扩展到举止、品味与轻蔑，描述一种人人可模仿的风格。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date and deeper origin): the earliest English use of the adjective is not precisely dated, and neither the make-up of aristos nor the pre-Greek origin of kratos is established.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代与更深词源）：形容词的最早英语用法没有确切年代；aristos 的构成与 kratos 在希腊语之前的来源均未得到证明。

note.en: Group one shares the arist- stem; group two holds adjectives of class and bearing.
note.cn: 第一组共享 arist- 词干；第二组是关于阶层与风度的形容词。

entries.definition: The class or the form of rule; the adjective describes a person or manner belonging to it.
entries.definitionCN: 阶层或统治形式；形容词描述属于它的人或风度。

entries.definition: One member of the class; the adjective could describe that member's bearing but not the member.
entries.definitionCN: 该阶层的一员；形容词可描述其风度，却不能指其人。

entries.definition: Of one-person rule, sharing -cratic but not the claim to be best.
entries.definitionCN: 指一人统治，共享 -cratic，却没有「最优」的主张。

entries.definition: Of rule by tested ability; it is often set against aristocratic as birth against merit.
entries.definitionCN: 指由被考核的能力统治；常与 aristocratic 对立，即出身对才能。

entries.definition: Of titled rank, or morally elevated; aristocratic stresses the class and its habits rather than virtue.
entries.definitionCN: 有头衔的，或品格高尚的；aristocratic 强调阶层及其习气，而非德性。

entries.definition: Of the hereditary upper class, originally the Roman senatorial families; narrower and more historical.
entries.definitionCN: 指世袭上层，原指罗马元老家族；更窄也更历史化。

entries.definition: Refined and respectable, often with a hint of pretending; it concerns manners only.
entries.definitionCN: 文雅体面，常带一点装样；只涉及举止。

entries.definition: The everyday compound for the top social layer; aristocratic adds heritage and style.
entries.definitionCN: 顶层社会的日常说法；aristocratic 另加世系与风格。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: aristos 'best' + -cratic 'ruling': originally about who should rule, later about who was born where.
normal.cn: aristos「最优」+ -cratic「统治的」：原问谁该统治，后来问谁生在哪里。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark manner more than birth: aristocratic bearing, aristocratic disdain, aristocratic taste.
normal.cn: 固定搭配更多标出风度而非出身：贵族气度、贵族式轻蔑、贵族品味。

normal.en: The family runs aristocracy, aristocrat, aristocratic, aristocratically.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 aristocracy、aristocrat、aristocratic、aristocratically。

normal.en: It pairs with its opposite: aristocratic birth against meritocratic examination.
normal.cn: 它与反义词配对：贵族出身对精英考试。

normal.en: The adverb names the manner: he refused aristocratically.
normal.cn: 副词指方式：他以贵族式的方式拒绝了。

abstract.en: Picture a straight back that has never once carried a chair.
abstract.cn: 想象一副挺直的背，从未搬过一把椅子。

abstract.en: Picture a slow voice that makes other people speed up.
abstract.cn: 想象一个缓慢的声音，让别人都快了起来。

abstract.en: Picture a door that is polite to everyone and open to almost no one.
abstract.cn: 想象一道对人人客气、却几乎不对任何人打开的门。

examples.en: The family kept an aristocratic reserve even after the estate was sold.
examples.cn: 庄园卖掉之后，这家人仍保持着贵族式的矜持。

examples.en: His aristocratic accent survived four years of factory work.
examples.cn: 四年的工厂生活也没磨掉他的贵族口音。

examples.en: Critics detected an aristocratic bias in the reading list.
examples.cn: 批评者在书单里看出一种贵族式的偏斜。

dict_mnemonic.text: aristo（最优）+ cratic（统治的）＝ 自认最优那一层的；记「背直、语慢、不搬椅」。

root: 希腊 aristos「最优」（其构成未获完整解释）+ kratos「力量」（希腊语之前的来源属重构形式）+ 形容词后缀 -ic；经法语进入英语。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from pedigree to posture: noble birth, noble bearing, noble rule, haughtiness, cultivated taste, the local upper set, exclusiveness, and a cultural claim to better standards.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从家谱走到姿态：贵族出身、贵族风度、贵族统治、高傲、有教养的品味、地方上层圈子、排他性，以及文化上主张更高标准。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a figure standing very straight on a stone step, speaking slowly, lifting nothing.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人笔直站在石阶上，说话很慢，什么也不搬。

branches.en: BIRTH AND OFFICE: the pedigree, then the constitution built on it.
branches.cn: 出身与职位：先是家谱，再是建立在它之上的政体。

branches.en: THE BODY SPEAKS: manner survives after title loses its power.
branches.cn: 身体在说话：头衔失权之后，风度仍在。

branches.en: THE VICE OF THE VIRTUE: assurance curdles into contempt.
branches.cn: 德性的毛病：笃定凝成了轻蔑。

branches.en: TASTE AND NEIGHBOURHOOD: cultivated style, and the local top set that shares it.
branches.cn: 品味与邻里：有教养的风格，以及共享它的地方上层。

branches.en: CLOSURE: the membership rule, and the cultural gate kept on standards.
branches.cn: 封闭：入会规则，以及以标准为名守着的文化之门。

intro.en: Aristocratic combines a Greek superlative, a Greek noun of power and an English adjective suffix; only the last is not Greek in origin.
intro.cn: aristocratic 合并希腊语最高级、希腊语「力量」名词与英语形容词后缀；只有最后一项不出希腊语。

latinIntro.en: The Greek elements reached English through Latin and French; kratos yields -cratic, and aristos appears nowhere else in English.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊成分经拉丁语与法语进入英语；kratos 给出 -cratic，aristos 在英语中不见于他处。

items.example: The word once meant best, not best born.
items.exampleCN: 这个词本指最优，而非出身最优。

items.meaning: of a named form of rule
items.example: Democratic and autocratic share this ending.
items.exampleCN: democratic 与 autocratic 共享这一词尾。

items.meaning: rule of the best; their class

items.example: The aristocrat sold the portrait quietly.
items.exampleCN: 那位贵族悄悄卖掉了肖像。
她以贵族式的方式点了点头。
精英考试取代了贵族人脉。
